items.title: Clozapine Augmentation Strategies and Clinical Predictors of Prolonged Tertiary Hospitalization in Clozapine-Resistant Schizophrenia: a Retrospective Cohort Study.
items.authors: Baldwin K, Honer WG, Shahbazi R, Fredrikson D, White RF, Villa-Rodriguez F, Rafizadeh R.

sections.heading: Background and hypothesis
sections.text: Clozapine-resistant schizophrenia (CRS) remains a major clinical challenge, with persistent symptoms and functional impairment despite adequate clozapine treatment. Real-world evidence is limited, and guidelines recommend a narrow set of augmentation strategies-aripiprazole (D2/3R partial agonist), amisulpride (D2/3R selective antagonist), and electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)-without clear guidance on selection or sequencing. This study examined augmentation choice and its association with length of stay (LOS) and symptomatic outcomes.

sections.heading: Study design
sections.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using BC Psychosis Program electronic records (2012-2025). Symptom severity and functioning scores (PANSS, CGI-S, GAPS, SOFAS) were extracted at admission and discharge. Multivariable Cox models assessed LOS for index and discharge augmentation strategies. ANCOVA compared symptom change across discharge strategies. A machine-learning model examined predictors of ECT versus pharmacological augmentation at discharge.

sections.heading: Study results
sections.text: Eighty-eight admissions were included. In adjusted index models, D2/3R selective antagonism was associated with shorter LOS than ECT (HR 2.50, 95% CI 1.35-4.62); partial agonism was not (HR 1.41, 95% CI 0.75-2.63). Partial agonist augmentation had the highest inefficacy-related switching. By discharge strategy, ECT was associated with greater reduction in positive symptoms than selective antagonism (MD -3.20, 95% CI -5.65 to -0.75) and partial agonism (MD -3.87, 95% CI -6.57 to -1.16). Greater impairment in psychosis and functioning on admission predicted ECT at discharge (AUC 0.74; balanced accuracy 0.72).

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: D2/3R selective antagonism was the most resource-efficient strategy, while ECT produced greater improvement in positive symptoms. Incorporating baseline psychosis severity and functioning into measurement-based care may support more informed augmentation selection.

items.title: Neurometabolic Differences in Psychosis Observed with 7 T Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy.
items.authors: Schallmo MP, Demro C, Killebrew KW, Sheldon AA, Olman CA, Sponheim SR, Marjańska M.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Altered brain chemistry is thought to contribute to impaired cognition and perceptual functioning in people with psychotic psychopathology (PwPP). As heritable genetic factors shape the development of psychosis, alterations in brain chemistry may extend to biological relatives of PwPP. Magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) is a non-invasive method for quantifying concentrations of various neurochemicals in the human brain. Previous studies using MRS have generally focused on specific diagnoses (eg, schizophrenia), rather than PwPP trans-diagnostically, and comparably few studies have examined relatives. The goal of the current study was to assess neurometabolic differences in PwPP and relatives using MRS in a large number of participants.

sections.heading: Study design
sections.text: As part of the Psychosis Human Connectome Project, we acquired ultra-short echo time (8 ms) MRS data at 7 tesla in both occipital and prefrontal cortices from 64 PwPP, 42 first-degree biological relatives, and 43 controls.

sections.heading: Study results
sections.text: We observed lower levels of N-acetyl-aspartate (NAA) in the occipital lobe in PwPP and relatives versus controls, and a trend toward lower N-acetyl-aspartylglutamate in prefrontal cortex in PwPP versus controls. Lower OCC NAA levels were also evident in diagnostic subgroups of PwPP (schizophrenia and bipolar disorder) compared to controls. We also observed higher levels of glucose in both occipital and prefrontal cortices in PwPP. Hierarchical clustering analyses showed that higher glucose levels were linked to higher psychiatric symptoms, poorer cognition, and impaired visual task performance.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Together, our findings point to alterations in neural metabolism across multiple brain areas in PwPP that are associated with impaired cognitive and perceptual functioning.

sections.heading: Importance
sections.text: Eating disorders are a major cause of nonfatal mental health burden, yet global evidence on their long-term trends, geographic distribution, and future trajectories remains limited.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To estimate the global, regional, and national prevalence and disability burden of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa-and mortality attributable to anorexia nervosa-from 1990 to 2023, and to forecast prevalence to 2050.

sections.heading: Design, setting, and participants
sections.text: Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 methods, data were synthesized from systematic literature reviews, population surveys, and vital registration systems. Estimates were produced for 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts through 2050. These data were analyzed from October 2025 to August 2026.

sections.heading: Exposure
sections.text: Anorexia nervosa or bulimia nervosa diagnosis.

sections.heading: Main outcomes and measures
sections.text: Counts and age-standardized rates with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs) for anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa prevalence, years lived with disability (YLDs), and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), and anorexia nervosa mortality, reported by age, sex, and location.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: In 2023, an estimated 18.1 million people (95% UI, 13.9-24.0) globally were living with anorexia nervosa or bulimia nervosa, of whom 12.6 million (69.4%) were female, 5.5 million were male (30.6%), and 41.2% were aged 10 to 24 years. These cases accounted for 3.83 million DALYs (95% UI, 2.23-5.69). Since 1990, the global number of prevalent cases increased by 71.0%, while age-standardized prevalence and DALY rates rose by about 21%. Females experienced substantially higher prevalence and DALY rates than males. The highest age-standardized prevalence rates were observed in high-income regions, particularly Australasia and Western Europe, whereas the largest relative increases in age-standardized prevalence occurred in East Asia, South Asia, and Southeast Asia. Forecasts indicate continued increases in prevalent cases through 2050.

sections.heading: Conclusions and relevance
sections.text: This GBD 2023 analysis found that anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa contribute substantially to global nonfatal health loss. These findings support the integration of eating disorders into mental health surveillance, prevention, and service planning worldwide.

items.title: Analysis and Prediction of Relapse Risk Factors in Community-Dwelling Individuals With Schizophrenia: Retrospective Cohort Study.
items.authors: Zhang W, Zhu D, Wang X, Li R, Jiang H, Liu Y, Cai J, Liu Z, Wang L.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Schizophrenia is a severe mental disorder characterized by high disability and relapse rates, posing significant challenges to public safety and community-based mental health management.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aimed to develop and validate a model for identifying hospitalization-related severe relapse risk among individuals with schizophrenia and to determine the key factors associated with this risk.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A total of 44,804 electronic records of community-managed individuals with schizophrenia were extracted from an information management system between January 1, 2022, and December 31, 2023. The dataset included demographic information, clinical records, interview data, policy support, and management indicators to construct a comprehensive feature system. A Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) machine learning algorithm was used for model development, with cost-sensitive learning applied to address class imbalance. Model interpretability was enhanced using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) to identify the most influential predictors of relapse risk.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: After screening, a total of 39,818 community-dwelling individuals with schizophrenia were included in this study, of whom 3717 (9.33%) experienced hospitalization-related severe relapse. The dataset was randomly divided using stratified sampling into a training set (n=31,854, 80%) and an independent test set (n=7964, 20%). Among the 6 machine learning models evaluated, LightGBM showed leading and balanced performance, yielding an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.95, an area under the precision-recall curve of 0.79, a relapse-class recall of 0.77, a precision of 0.71, and an F _1-score of 0.74 in the independent test set. SHAP-based interpretability analysis identified medication persistence (23.30%), specialist recommendation: medication adherence training (19.74%), number of follow-ups (7.38%), age (3.72%), and educational attainment (3.58%) as the most influential predictors. items.title: Content Validity and Psychometric Properties Assessment of the Virtual Reality Functional Capacity Assessment Tool and Application in Multiregional Clinical Trials of Cognitive Impairment Associated with Schizophrenia.
items.authors: Klein H, Horan WP, Clarke N, Howells FM, Cocks K, Daskalopoulou C, Pascoe B, Reaney M, Langevin N, Fowler JC, Tang W, Harvey PD, Keefe RSE.

sections.heading: Background and hypothesis
sections.text: Cognitive impairment associated with schizophrenia (CIAS) substantially impacts daily living and is a valuable prognostic indicator of functional outcomes in people living with schizophrenia. The Virtual Reality Functional Capacity Assessment Tool (VRFCAT) is used to assess functional capacity, facilitating the development of new treatments for cognitive impairment. This paper aims to provide evidence supporting the use of the VRFCAT as a valid and reliable performance outcome measure to assess functional change (ie, a fit-for-purpose clinical outcome assessment instrument).

sections.heading: Study design
sections.text: This paper is divided into two parts. In Part 1, published and unpublished evidence regarding the suitability of the VRFCAT is synthesized, focusing on content validity, including concept mapping to an updated CIAS conceptual model informed by patient input and evaluation, and known psychometric properties. In Part 2, data collected from three multinational CIAS clinical trials are used to evaluate additional psychometric properties (practice effects, test-retest, and convergent validity) and assess the utility of the VRFCAT within its intended context of use.

sections.heading: Study results
sections.text: Published literature supports content validity and key psychometric properties of the VRFCAT. The VRFCAT demonstrates alignment with the signs, symptoms, and impacts in the CIAS conceptual model. Analysis of clinical trial data substantiates published psychometric properties within the intended context of use, with no practice effects identified.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: These findings provide evidence that the VRFCAT is a valid and reliable performance outcome measure for use in assessing functional capacity in people with CIAS, supporting its suitability for use in clinical trials.

items.title: Predicting Depressive Symptoms From Cross-Sectional and Longitudinal Data Using XGBoost-SHAP and Cross-Lagged Model.
items.authors: Jie J, Yin M, Zeng J, Yang S.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: University students face significant academic, social, and career-planning challenges. Under such stressors, deficient emotion regulation may increase vulnerability to depressive states, in which persistent symptoms could progress to clinical depression. This study investigates key risk and protective factors for depressive symptoms among university students, including negative life events, neuroticism, and social support. A longitudinal framework was further employed to assess changes in depressive symptoms before and after the COVID-19 pandemic, with the goal of informing early identification and intervention strategies.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The dataset included 18 024 valid responses from baseline assessments. Follow-up assessments conducted 1 year later included 6129 participants. The extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used to quantify the relative importance of specific factors (e.g., negative life events and social support) on depressive symptoms, while a cross-lagged panel model examined longitudinal directional associations between these factors and depressive symptoms.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The prevalence of depressive symptoms was 15.2% among the student sample. Significant correlations were observed between symptom severity and adverse family relationships, childhood trauma, prior suicide attempts, and psychiatric history. Neuroticism and negative life events showed significant positive associations with depressive symptoms, while subjective support and support utilization demonstrated negative associations with symptom severity. Longitudinal analysis revealed an increase in both symptom severity and depression detection rates following the COVID-19 pandemic. The cross-lagged panel model identified neuroticism as a significant positive longitudinal predictor of depressive symptoms, whereas subjective support showed a significant negative longitudinal association with subsequent depressive symptoms.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: This study identifies neuroticism as an important longitudinal risk indicator for depressive symptoms and subjective support as a protective indicator, while negative life events showed significant cross-sectional associations with symptom severity. The findings demonstrate how integrating longitudinal designs with interpretable machine learning elucidates complex mental health dynamics in student populations, providing an evidence-based framework for targeted interventions within campus mental health policies.

items.title: Relationship between upward social comparison and adolescent depression: moderating roles of football participation.
items.authors: Zheng Y, Huang H, Li A, Zhong C, Zhang L, Shui Y.

sections.text: Adolescent depression is an important global public health concern. Although sport participation is generally associated with better mental health among adolescents, it remains unclear whether it moderates the association between upward social comparison and depressive symptoms and whether this effect differs across sport types. To address this gap, this study aimed to examine whether sport participation moderates the association and whether the effect differs between football participants and participants in individual sports. A total of 2,451 adolescents were recruited from 162 schools across 13 provinces in China; after excluding 16 participants, 2,435 were included in the final analyses (age, M = 12.36, SD = 3.42). Participants completed the Upward Social Comparison Scale, the Sports Participation Scale, and the Beck Depression Inventory-II. Using Hayes' PROCESS macro (Models 1 and 3), this study assessed moderation while controlling for gender and school level. Upward social comparison was positively associated with depression (b = 0.079, p < 0.001), while sport participation was negatively associated with depression (b = -0.155, p < 0.001). Their interaction was significant (b = -0.055, p = 0.005), indicating that higher sport participation was associated with a weaker positive association between upward social comparison and depression. A three-way interaction was also significant (b = 0.163, p = 0.002), indicating that the moderation pattern differed by sport type. Among football participants, the positive association between upward social comparison and depression was weaker at higher levels of sport participation but remained statistically significant, whereas no significant association was observed at either level of sport participation among participants in individual sports. In conclusion, higher levels of sport participation were associated with a weaker positive association between upward social comparison and adolescent depression, and this moderation pattern differed by sport type. These findings may inform public health strategies that consider football-based activities as a promising context for adolescent mental health promotion.

items.title: Suicide mortality in Kazakhstan from 2012 to 2024: temporal trends, demographic inequalities, and regional variation.
items.authors: Kossumov A, Zhakupova T, Imambayeva N, Polyakova T, Dalibayeva G, Syzdykova B, Kovenskiy A, Rakhmankulova A, Vinogradova E, Kalmakhanov S, Kozhakhmetov S, Kushugulova A.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Despite some recent declines, suicides remain a major public health issue in Kazakhstan, with rates persistently above global benchmarks. This study provides the first integrated characterization of temporal trends, demographic characteristics, and regional distribution of suicide mortality in Kazakhstan.

sections.heading: Materials and methods
sections.text: This epidemiological analysis examined suicide mortality data over a 13-year period (2012-2024). Data were provided by the Republican State Enterprise "Forensic Examination Center of the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Kazakhstan" and the State Institution "Committee on Legal Statistics and Special Records of the Prosecutor General's Office.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Between 2012 and 2024, 46,546 suicides were registered in Kazakhstan. Absolute suicides decreased by 15.8% despite 19.3% population growth. By 2023-2024, SR = 17.8 (ASSR = 18.2) - more than 65% above the WHO global average. The male-to-female ratio was 3.8:1 (ASSRs: men 29.9, women 7.4). Among men, peaks occurred at 25-29 (SR = 38.6) and 45-54 (SR = 49.9); among women, the first peak was at 18-24 (SR = 10.6). Regional SRs ranged from 11.0 to 29.2 per 100,000. The aging index was the strongest demographic ecological correlate of regional SR ( r  = 0.84, p  ≤ 0.0001). Annual sunshine duration showed a significant inverse association with SR ( β  = -0.814, 95% CI [-1.221; -0.407], p  = 0.001) in the regional regression model, while average salary was not significant.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Regional demographic restructuring - particularly population aging concentrated in northern regions - is the primary structural correlate of regional suicide variability. Annual sunshine duration emerged as a significant ecological correlate in the regression model specifically testing environmental and economic factors. These findings provide an evidence base for targeted, region- and population-specific prevention measures.

items.title: Weaponizing the Bond: Pet Abuse as a Mediator of IPV Victimization and Mental Health Symptomology.
items.authors: Renken ND, Spencer CM, Moore MM.

sections.text: Objective: The purpose of the current study was to understand how the perpetration of pet abuse (i.e., dog and cat), in the context of intimate partner violence (IPV), contributes to victims' mental health outcomes. We were specifically interested in examining 1) the relationship between a partner's pet abuse perpetration and depression, anxiety, and PTSD and 2) how pet abuse might mediate the relationship between IPV victimization and mental health outcomes. Method: Participants (N = 1,173) were recruited online via TestSet and responded to items related to IPV victimization, their partner's maltreatment of dogs or cats, and current mental health symptomology. Separate path models estimated the direct and indirect effects of physical, psychological, and sexual IPV victimization on depression, anxiety, and PTSD symptoms, with a partner's cat and dog abuse specified as mediators. Results: Psychological IPV victimization and pet abuse consistently emerged as the strongest direct predictors of mental health symptomology across all models. Dog and cat abuse significantly mediated the relationships between physical and sexual IPV, but not psychological IPV, on victims' depressive, anxiety, and PTSD symptoms. Conclusions: Pet abuse is a significant risk marker for IPV and psychological distress. Pet abuse warrants both legal recognition as a form of domestic violence and clinical recognition as a distinct source of trauma.

items.title: Anxiety and Coping Strategies in Caregivers of Children With Epidermal Differentiation Disorders: A Case-Control Study.
items.authors: Fryze M, Pietrzak A, Mlak R, Wawrzycki B, Wertheim-Tysarowska K, van Veen FCAP, Gostynski AH.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Epidermal differentiation disorders (EDDs) are rare, chronic skin diseases with significant psychosocial impact on patients and families. Their daily management requires complex care, placing caregivers at risk of stress and anxiety. Few studies have systematically examined anxiety and coping strategies in this group.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: To compare anxiety levels and coping styles between caregivers of children with syndromic or nonsyndromic EDD and caregivers of healthy children.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In this cross-sectional case-control study, 39 caregivers of children with EDD and 39 matched controls were recruited from a dermatology clinic. Anxiety was assessed with the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) and coping styles with the Coping Inventory for Stressful Situations (CISS). Sociodemographic and clinical data were collected.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Caregivers of children with EDDs reported significantly higher trait anxiety than controls (79.5% vs. 53.8%; p = 0.017). Task-oriented coping (TOC) was less frequent among EDD caregivers, with more than half showing low TOC compared with less than one-third of controls (56.4% vs. 28.6%; p = 0.019). High avoidance-oriented coping (AOC) was observed more often in controls (21.4% vs. 5.6%; p = 0.044). Anxiety was greater among caregivers of boys than girls (95.7% vs. 56.2%; p = 0.003). Avoidant coping was associated with greater child symptom severity, including pruritus and redness.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Caregivers of children with EDD experience high anxiety and rely less on adaptive coping strategies. These findings emphasize the need for early, family-centered psychosocial interventions to support caregiver well-being and improve outcomes for affected children.

items.title: eHealth Literacy and Depressive Symptoms Among Adults Aged 50 Years and Older in China: A National Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Zhou Q, Guo S, Jing R.

sections.text: Despite existing research confirming that eHealth literacy promotes healthy lifestyles and subjective well-being among adults aged 50 years and older, its connection to depressive symptoms remains unclear. This cross-sectional study explored the association between eHealth literacy and depressive symptoms among adults aged 50 years and older, and investigated potential mechanisms and moderating effects of the association. Data were obtained from the China Digital Divide and Digital Inclusion Survey (CDDDIS), which provided a nationally representative sample of 4284 participants aged 50 years and older. Ordinary least squares (OLS) regression was employed to analyze the associations between eHealth literacy and depressive symptoms, adjusting for relevant sociodemographic and health-related covariates. Bootstrap-based mediation analysis was conducted to evaluate indirect pathways embedded within the correlation network. Income-stratified analyses were performed to explore differences in the association across income groups. The results revealed that higher eHealth literacy was significantly correlated with fewer depressive symptoms (β = -0.029, 95% CI = [-0.052, -0.006], p = 0.012). Bootstrapped mediation analysis revealed that physical activity and perceived stress served as significant indirect pathways mediating the association in this correlational analysis, whereas the indirect pathway via online healthcare services utilization was not statistically significant. Income-stratified analysis showed that the negative association between eHealth literacy and depressive symptoms was statistically significant among middle- and high-income participants, whereas no significant association was observed for low-income participants. eHealth literacy constitutes a critical resource for promoting healthy aging and mitigating aging-related stressors among adults aged 50 years and older. These correlational patterns suggest potential utility for targeted eHealth interventions aimed at reducing depressive symptoms in aging populations.

items.title: Bipolar disorder and risk of all-cause and specific dementia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.authors: Gao Z, Ren M, Yang R, Yu J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Bipolar disorder (BD) is associated with cognitive impairment and an increased risk of dementia; however, the magnitude of this association and subtype-specific risk patterns remain unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis quantified the associations between BD and the risks of all-cause dementia, Alzheimer's disease (AD), and vascular dementia (VaD), and explored potential sources of between-study heterogeneity.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to September 15, 2026. Eligible cohort and case-control studies reported adjusted effect estimates for the association between BD and dementia. Hazard ratios and odds ratios were converted to risk ratios (RRs) prior to quantitative synthesis. Random- or fixed-effects models were applied according to heterogeneity. Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses, Egger's test for publication bias, and subgroup analyses stratified by follow-up duration, sex, age at BD onset, and study design were conducted.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Eleven studies involving 1,536,508 participants and 90,864 all-cause dementia cases were included. BD was associated with an increased risk of all-cause dementia (RR = 3.55, 95% CI 2.48-5.07; I^2 = 98.7%), AD (RR = 5.08, 95% CI 1.87-13.84; I^2 = 97.2%), and VaD (RR = 4.33, 95% CI 3.06-6.13; I^2 = 71.7%). Estimates for all-cause dementia and VaD were robust in sensitivity analyses, whereas the AD estimate was sensitive to the exclusion of individual studies and should therefore be interpreted cautiously. The association between BD and increased dementia risk was observed across the examined subgroups. Formal tests for subgroup differences showed no statistically significant differences according to sex or age at BD onset.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: BD is associated with an increased risk of all-cause dementia, AD, and VaD. However, substantial between-study heterogeneity and the limited evidence available for specific dementia subtypes warrant cautious interpretation of the pooled estimates. Further high-quality longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the factors underlying heterogeneity and subtype-specific associations.

Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses, Egger's test for publication bias, and subgroup analyses stratified by follow-up duration, sex, age at BD onset, and study design were conducted.

Eleven studies involving 1,536,508 participants and 90,864 all-cause dementia cases were included. BD was associated with an increased risk of all-cause dementia (RR = 3.55, 95% CI 2.48-5.07; I^2 = 98.7%), AD (RR = 5.08, 95% CI 1.87-13.84; I^2 = 97.2%), and VaD (RR = 4.33, 95% CI 3.06-6.13; I^2 = 71.7%). Estimates for all-cause dementia and VaD were robust in sensitivity analyses, whereas the AD estimate was sensitive to the exclusion of individual studies and should therefore be interpreted cautiously. The association between BD and increased dementia risk was observed across the examined subgroups. Formal tests for subgroup differences showed no statistically significant differences according to sex or age at BD onset.

BD is associated with an increased risk of all-cause dementia, AD, and VaD. However, substantial between-study heterogeneity and the limited evidence available for specific dementia subtypes warrant cautious interpretation of the pooled estimates. Further high-quality longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the factors underlying heterogeneity and subtype-specific associations.

items.title: Examining the links between vitamin C and schizophrenia spectrum disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis on circulating levels and supplementation outcomes.
items.authors: Suresh G, Chengaiyan JG, Dabaghzadeh F, Ahmad F.

sections.text: Schizophrenia (SCZ) is a debilitating psychiatric condition characterized by psychotic symptoms such as hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized thought. Recent evidence suggests its association with deficiency of various micronutrients. Vitamin C (vitC) is a key endogenous metabolite with potent antioxidant and neuroprotectant actions. However, the relationship between vitC deficiency and SCZ remains inconclusively established, both at the epidemiological and clinical levels, hindering its potential utility as a biomarker and a supplementary therapeutic. The purpose of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to investigate whether circulating levels of endogenous vitC are altered in SCZ subjects, and to examine the effect of exogenous vitC supplements on disease outcomes. Systematic searches for pertinent primary peer-reviewed studies on scholarly databases identified 19 studies. Newcastle-Ottawa scale and Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies were applied to judge the quality of studies of the case-control and supplementation trials, respectively. Random-effects restricted maximum likelihood meta-analysis models were employed for addressing the two specific aims of the study using standardized mean difference (SMD) as the point estimate. SCZ patients showed significantly lowered vitC levels compared to the controls, with the pooled SMD being -1.046 [-1.459, -0.632]. Further, vitC supplementation was found to significantly reduce psychotic symptoms by -1.632 [-2.473, -0.791] units across a total of 6 datasets. VitC deficiency appears to be a consistent feature of SCZ across diverse populations and its supplementation may be considered as a safe, inexpensive adjunct to antipsychotic therapy.

items.title: GABAergic Network Dysregulation in Alcohol Use Disorder: Receptor-Transporter Interactions Driving the Transition From Goal-Directed to Compulsive Behaviour.
items.authors: Aranda H, Jones N, Haroon H, Choi DS.

sections.text: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is characterized by a shift from controlled, goal-directed drinking to compulsive, habitual alcohol (a.k.a. ethanol) seeking, even in the face of negative outcomes. This transition is closely associated with alterations in cortico-striatal circuitry and dysregulated GABAergic signalling, both of which drive the progression from flexible control to compulsive behaviour. Acute alcohol exposure enhances GABAergic inhibition, primarily by increasing presynaptic GABA release. Chronic exposure leads to compensatory neuroadaptations, such as subunit reorganization, receptor internalization and diminished GABA receptor sensitivity. While these neuroadaptations alter receptor-mediated GABAergic signalling during dependence and withdrawal, they also alter dopaminergic regulation and further reinforce alcohol-seeking behaviour. Beyond receptor-level adaptations, impaired GABA clearance, especially through the astrocytic transporter GAT3, plays a crucial role in regulating extracellular GABA concentrations and tonic inhibition. This effect is particularly evident within the dorsal striatum, where elevated tonic GABA shifts control from flexible, goal-directed action towards rigid, habitual responding by altering the balance between the dorsomedial and dorsolateral subregions. Consistent with these mechanistic insights, animal and human studies demonstrate that reduced GAT3 expression is associated with compulsive alcohol use and impaired reward-related behaviour, reinforcing impaired GABA clearance as a central mechanism in this behavioural shift. Taken together, these lines of evidence validate a central therapeutic model, namely, that targeting altered tonic inhibition and impaired GABA clearance in AUD could address the inhibitory dysfunction that sustains the disorder. Overall, this work supports a unifying model in which receptor adaptations and disrupted GABA removal maintain altered inhibitory tone, driving maladaptive circuit function and contributing to the persistence of AUD.

items.title: Associations of mental health, substance use and housing instability with hospitalisation outcomes for adults with diabetes complications: a retrospective cohort study in Maryland, USA.
items.authors: Qureshi N, Azimian S, Matthias J, Kharrazi H.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Mental health disorders (MH), substance use disorder (SUD) and housing instability (HI) are frequently co-occurring vulnerabilities that complicate diabetes self-management, contributing to healthcare utilisation. However, limited research has examined their combined associations with hospitalisation outcomes among patients admitted for diabetes-related complications. We evaluated the individual and joint associations of MH, SUD and HI with emergency department-initiated admission (ED-IA) and 30-day, 60-day and 90-day readmission.

sections.heading: Research design and methods
sections.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Maryland statewide hospital discharge data repository (2016-2023). Patients aged ≥18 years with an index hospitalisation for diabetes complications were included. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted ORs (aORs) for the associations of MH, SUD and HI with ED-IA and readmission, adjusting for demographic, socioeconomic and clinical characteristics. Exposures were modelled individually and as composite categories to characterise associations for observed co-occurrence patterns.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among 48 308 patients, 45.2% had MH, 34.3% had SUD and 1.3% had HI. Readmission occurred in 4.8%, 7.8% and 10.3% at 30, 60 and 90 days; 87.9% of index admissions originated in the ED. MH was associated with ED-IA (aOR 1.31) and readmission (30-day aOR 1.61; 60-day aOR 1.56; 90-day aOR 1.53). SUD was not associated with ED-IA but was associated with readmission (aORs 1.51, 1.63 and 1.70). HI was associated with ED-IA (aOR 1.68) but not readmission. Patients with all three vulnerabilities had the highest odds of ED-IA (aOR 2.84) and readmission (aORs 2.93, 2.78 and 3.15).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: MH, SUD and HI were independently and jointly associated with increased healthcare utilisation (ED-IA and readmission) among adults hospitalised for diabetes complications. These findings underscore the need for prospective research to evaluate whether integrated diabetes care models incorporating behavioural health interventions and housing support into comprehensive discharge planning reduce ED utilisation and hospital readmissions.

items.title: Amygdala volume and psychiatric burden in focal epilepsy: PET evidence for a glial substrate.
items.authors: Imhoff-Smith TP, McMillan A, Hurley SA, Kalkach Aparicio M, Nair V, Philibert-Rosas S, Binder JR, Meyerand ME, Jones J, Hermann B, Prabhakaran V, Adluru N, Struck AF.

sections.text: Temporal lobe epilepsy is of heterogeneous pathology. While many patients present with hippocampal sclerosis and ipsilateral mesiotemporal atrophy, a subgroup of patients without human-detectable sclerosis via structural MRI are characterized by ipsilateral amygdala enlargement and worse postsurgical outcomes. A bidirectional relationship between temporal lobe epilepsy and depression is well-established, with amygdala enlargement and neuroimmune alterations increasingly implicated as substrates for both. In this study, we interrogate the link between amygdala volume and psychiatric burden in temporal lobe epilepsy and evaluate gliosis as a possible substrate. We hypothesize that gliosis drives ipsilateral amygdala volume changes that underlie psychiatric burden in patients with no hippocampal sclerosis. To test these relationships, we analyzed two independent cross-sectional cohorts: (i) a Discovery cohort (43 patients, 80 controls) with structural MRI and robust psychiatric measures and (ii) a Mechanistic pilot cohort (10 patients, 9 controls) with both structural MRI and [^18F]FEPPA PET/MR, an in vivo measure of gliosis, to conceptually replicate and extend findings from the Discovery cohort. Amygdala volumes were assessed with FreeSurfer. Psychiatric burden in the Discovery cohort was assessed with the Depressive Problems subscale from the Achenbach Adult Self-Report. Regional gliosis in the Mechanistic cohort was quantified using [^18F]FEPPA PET, and an exploratory measure of psychiatric burden for this cohort was obtained via medical chart review. In the Discovery cohort, the group without hippocampal sclerosis showed significant ipsilateral enlargement of the whole amygdala, basolateral and central subnuclei compared to controls and the group with sclerosis and a group-dependent association between decreased amygdala volume and increased depressive symptoms. In the Mechanistic cohort, increased [^18F]FEPPA binding was associated with reduced amygdala volume. Adjusting for this effect unmasked significant amygdala enlargement in the group without hippocampal sclerosis. Exploratory analysis revealed a possible central subnucleus-specific relationship between gliosis, volume and psychiatric burden in patients without sclerosis, such that amygdala volume was positively correlated with psychiatric burden specifically in patients with a greater degree of gliosis. These data associate amygdala volume alterations with psychiatric burden in patients without sclerosis and implicate gliosis as a potential mechanistic substrate. Findings support a conceptual shift towards understanding amygdala enlargement not as a static structural phenotype, but as a dynamic, glia-associated state that may confer risk for psychiatric illness. Consequently, patients without hippocampal sclerosis may derive a distinct dual benefit from therapeutic strategies targeted at underlying neuroimmune function.

items.title: Liquid Compared to Solid Oral Formulations of the Thyroid Hormone Receptor Agonist Elunetirom Under Fasted and Fed Conditions in Healthy Participants.
items.authors: Harris JR, van Haarst AD, Baccei J, Franey B, Everett J, George K, Paglialunga S, Webster K, Hillstrand M, Banfield C, Scanlan TS, Davar G.

sections.text: Elunetirom (ABX-002) is a brain-targeted, oral prodrug being developed for the adjunctive treatment of major depressive disorder and bipolar depression. The active moiety, LL-340001, is a thyroid hormone receptor agonist with modest selectivity for beta over alpha thyroid hormone receptors. Upon entering the brain, the intended site of action, elunetirom is hydrolyzed by fatty acid amide hydrolase to LL-340001. In this 3-way randomized, crossover, bioequivalence study, the pharmacokinetics (PK) and safety of an oral liquid formulation used in early clinical development were compared with those of an oral solid formulation intended for later-stage development and potential commercialization, under fasted and fed conditions. Healthy adult participants received single doses of elunetirom (45 μg) as a liquid formulation under fasted conditions and as a solid formulation under fasted conditions and 30 min after consumption of a high-fat meal. Administration of the solid formulation under fasted conditions resulted in elunetirom and LL-340001 exposures similar to those observed with the liquid formulation and is therefore considered to have comparative bioavailability. Food intake increased elunetirom total exposure (AUC) compared with the fasted state but did not affect maximum exposure (C_max). In contrast, administration with food reduced LL-340001 C_max compared with the fasted state but did not affect AUC. Food intake delayed the time to reach C_max (T_max) for both elunetirom and LL-340001. Elunetirom, administered orally as a liquid and as a solid formulation, was safe and well tolerated under fed and fasted conditions.

items.title: Brexpiprazole in India and the United States: A Comparative Review of Regulatory Status, Clinical Evidence, Market Access, and Evidence Gaps.
items.authors: Gill N, Sohi SK, Bhatti N, Joseph G, Abhilasha P.

sections.text: Brexpiprazole is a serotonin-dopamine activity modulator first cleared by the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2015 for adults with schizophrenia and as an adjunct to antidepressants in major depressive disorder (MDD); later authorizations extended its use to adolescent schizophrenia and to agitation arising in dementia due to Alzheimer's disease. Over the past decade, randomized controlled trials, long-term open-label extensions, and analyses of real-world claims have converged on a consistent efficacy profile and a tolerability profile that has generally been favorable, although direct head-to-head comparisons with other second-generation agents remain limited. The evidence base and access environment differ markedly between the two countries. In the United States, brexpiprazole is an established product with an extensive clinical evidence base supplemented by real-world claims, utilization, safety, and economic analyses. In contrast, India has only recently received regulatory approval for brexpiprazole, and brexpiprazole-specific clinical, real-world utilization, pricing, reimbursement, and pharmacoeconomic data remain limited. This narrative review consolidates the pharmacology, clinical-trial findings, safety record, and health-economic data on brexpiprazole and contrasts the mature evidence environment of the United States with the emerging one in India. The principal Indian evidence gap is therefore no longer regulatory recognition but the generation of local data on availability, affordability, utilization, effectiveness, and pharmacoeconomic value. Framed as a collaboration between Christian Medical College and Hospital, Ludhiana, and New York Medical College at St Clare's and St Mary's, New Jersey, the review aims to support the equitable and evidence-based uptake of newer antipsychotics in emerging settings.

items.title: Severe and Prolonged Paroxetine Intoxication With Delayed Absorption and Extreme Serum Concentrations: A Case Report.
items.authors: Beijnsberger L, Boly CA, Jaspers TC, Van Oers JA.

sections.text: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are commonly prescribed antidepressants, known for their relatively safe pharmacological profile and mild symptoms in cases of overdose compared with other antidepressants. In this case report, we describe a near-fatal case of a 70-year-old woman who ingested multiple drugs with suicidal intent, including an unknown quantity of celecoxib 200 mg, clorazepate acid 5 mg, omeprazole 20 mg, and immediate-release paroxetine 30 mg tablets. The patient developed severe serotonin syndrome complicated by acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and required admission to the intensive care unit (ICU). Because of progressive respiratory deterioration, she required intubation and invasive mechanical ventilation. Serotonin syndrome persisted for an unusually long period, with serum paroxetine concentrations of 4805 µg/L at admission that continued to rise to a maximum of 7824 µg/L on day four, both well above the lethal threshold. Intensive therapeutic interventions aimed at lowering paroxetine concentrations and resolving serotonin syndrome included activated charcoal, whole-bowel irrigation lavage, and rifampicin. Paroxetine concentrations gradually declined and reached the therapeutic range after 16 days. Following further ICU treatment, including prone ventilation and corticosteroids, the ARDS resolved, and the patient was extubated 21 days after ingestion. This case highlights that paroxetine overdose may present more severely than commonly reported in the literature, with delayed and prolonged toxicity, including serotonin syndrome and ARDS. Paroxetine overdose may be life-threatening and underscores the need for close monitoring of serum paroxetine concentrations and timely consideration of activated charcoal and whole-bowel irrigation.

items.title: Supporting adolescents with self-harm: practitioners' experiences of delivering a rapid brief psychological intervention to adolescents presenting to Emergency Departments.
items.authors: O'Keeffe S, Long M, Saour T, McCabe R.
items.journal: Frontiers in child and adolescent psychiatry

sections.text: The risk of suicide is increased amongst young people following attendance at the Emergency Department (ED) for self-harm. Evidence is limited for effective interventions. Early intervention is crucial before self-harm becomes established as a coping mechanism. The Supporting Adolescents with Self-Harm (SASH) intervention focuses on supporting young peoples' agency and resources-comprising Therapeutic Assessment, Enhanced Safety Planning and Solution-Focused Follow-Up sessions-and was evaluated in a randomised controlled trial. To explore the experiences of CAMHS crisis team practitioners delivering the SASH intervention to young people presenting to EDs with self-harm in the SASH trial. The trial assessed the effectiveness of the SASH intervention. This study forms part of the qualitative process evaluation exploring the experiences of practitioners delivering the intervention. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 practitioners who delivered the intervention and four senior staff members. Interviews were analysed using thematic analysis. Six overarching themes were identified: (1) A transformation in practice, bridging the gap in crisis care by offering an immediate therapeutic intervention and time to build rapport and work with the system around young people; (2) Patient-centred care that builds shared understanding of the reasons underlying self-harm between the young person, carer and practitioner; (3) Harnessing young people's strengths and motivating change; (4) Carer involvement in individual/joint sessions leads to better outcomes when the young person wants them involved and they are available; (5) SASH worked well for most young people, although it may be less suited to those who are less able to express themselves, or have complex difficulties or difficulties that are outside their control; and (6) At first, a paradigm shift for practitioners from focusing on problems to solutions, but over time practitioners gained confidence and motivation in using the SASH intervention and continue to use it in their practice. The SASH intervention offers continuity of care after ED attendance for young people following a self-harm crisis by focusing on building shared understanding of the underlying reasons for self-harm and harnessing their strengths, bridging the gap in crisis care. Supporting carers may also improve outcomes for young people. https://www.isrctn.com/, identifier ISRCTN81846131.

items.title: Predicting documented prior intentional self-harm in emergency departments: an interpretable gradient boosting approach using European injury surveillance data.
items.authors: Giustini M, Pitidis A, Fazio C, Alves T, Fian T, Valkenberg H, Nijman S, Papadakaki M, Carannante A.

sections.text: Prior intentional self-harm history is the strongest predictor of completed suicide, yet this information frequently goes uncommunicated during emergency department (ED) presentations. We developed an interpretable gradient boosting model (XGBoost) to predict whether a patient's record in the European Injury Database (EU-IDB) carries a documented prior self-harm flag, using injury characteristics, demographics, and clinical features available at ED attendance. The raw dataset comprised 62,467 attendances for intentional self-harm from 18 countries (2008-2023), with 86.2% of outcomes coded Unknown. Formal missingness analysis showed that observed outcome missingness was overwhelmingly explained by country membership (country alone: pseudo-R2 = 0.537, AUC = 0.948) and that documentation was positive-biased: across countries, the sparser the documentation, the higher the positivity among documented records (Spearman ρ = 0.882). A three-step "Third Way" strategy excluded three countries with structurally absent outcome protocols and defined the target as a documented positive flag vs. its absence, yielding an analytical dataset of 26,554 records (prevalence 13.7%), three times larger than the complete-case alternative. XGBoost achieved AUC-ROC = 0.800 (95% CI 0.783-0.816), AUC-PR = 0.380, and Brier score = 0.100, significantly outperforming logistic regression (DeLong p = 3.93 × 10-10). At the optimised threshold (0.080), sensitivity was 80.8%, specificity 62.8%, NPV 95.4%. A time-zero model restricted to variables available at triage achieved AUC-ROC = 0.762 (0.745-0.780) and retained its advantage over the linear baseline (0.729, 0.712-0.746). SHAP analysis identified proximal risk factor documentation, place of occurrence, and patient age as dominant predictors, and a sensitivity analysis excluding the ProximalRiskFactor variable (AUC-ROC = 0.765) confirmed robustness to a potentially circular feature. A country prediction test (95.3% accuracy, 14.3× chance) quantified substantial implicit geographic encoding in the clinical features, offering a plausible explanation for the gap between test-set AUC-ROC (0.800), temporal validation (0.674) and group-aware cross-validation (0.658). Country-stratified assessment revealed adequate calibration in most settings but miscalibration in low-volume countries, and fairness analysis identified lower sensitivity in older adults (68.0%; AUC-ROC 0.722, 95% CI 0.617-0.822) as a critical limitation. This model could serve as a decision support layer within ED workflows, but requires local validation, country-specific recalibration, and embedding within structured post-identification care pathways before deployment.

items.title: Mapping the natural course of comorbid bipolar disorder via integration of multimodal data (MapCoBD): a study protocol.
items.authors: Comai S, Morena M, Steardo L, Squassina A, Pisanu C, Meloni A, Congiu D, Lazzardi S, Pinna M, Contu M, Nasini S, Barzon B, Zuliani AM, Dall'Acqua S, Balestrieri A, Campolongo P, Pullano I, Iazzolino AM, de Filippis R, Pinna F, Saba L, Manchia M.

sections.text: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a chronic, disabling psychiatric condition with a high global disease burden. Its course is marked by alternating episodes of mania and depression, with varying degrees of severity. While cyclicity is a defining feature, clinical patterns show significant inter-individual and intra-individual variability. Although naturalistic studies have described the course of BD, the impact of psychiatric comorbidities, particularly attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and borderline personality disorder (BPD), remains underexplored. MapCoBD is a 12-month, naturalistic observational study whose primary objective is to compare the longitudinal clinical course of BD among individuals with classic episodic BD, BD with comorbid ADHD, and BD with comorbid BPD. Secondary objectives are to characterize the clinical, neuropsychological, neuroimaging, and molecular features associated with these distinct clinical courses. This project will recruit 150 BD individuals divided into three groups: (1) classic episodic BD (epiBD, n = 50), (2) BD with comorbid ADHD (BD-ADHD, n = 50), and (3) BD with comorbid BPD (BD-BPD, n = 50). Assessments will be conducted at baseline (T0), 6 months (T1), and 12 months (T2), including: mood symptom ratings, neuropsychological testing, fasting blood sampling (for serum, plasma, and microRNA), and 3T structural brain MRI scans. Daily mood ratings will also be collected prospectively throughout the study. The primary longitudinal clinical endpoint will be illness burden, defined as the proportion of evaluable follow-up days spent with moderate-to-severe psychopathological symptoms, based on prospective NIMH Life Chart Method assessments. Daily affective ratings will additionally be used to characterize mood instability. At each time point, peripheral biomarkers implicated in BD pathophysiology, including endocannabinoid (eCB) signaling, inflammatory cascade (IC), and epigenetic regulation (microRNA), will be quantified. Clinical, neuroimaging, and molecular data will also be integrated using supervised machine-learning approaches to explore the classification of clinical group status and the prediction of longitudinal mood instability and illness burden. This study will determine whether ADHD and BPD comorbidity is associated with distinct longitudinal patterns of illness burden and mood instability in BD. The integration of clinical, neuroimaging, and molecular data may identify group-specific multimodal signatures and candidate predictors of clinical course, which will require independent validation before clinical application.

items.title: Clinical deterioration after revisiting childhood sexual abuse during psychotherapy for restrictive anorexia nervosa: a case report.
items.authors: Cirillo F, Bozzola E, Spina G, Irrera M, Marchesi A, Marotta R, Marchili MR.

sections.text: Childhood traumatic experiences are increasingly recognized as important contributors to the development and maintenance of eating disorders. In adolescents with anorexia nervosa (AN), traumatic experiences may interact with restrictive symptoms through mechanisms involving emotional dysregulation, avoidance, and maladaptive control strategies. However, the optimal timing and approach for addressing traumatic experiences in severely underweight adolescents with AN remain unclear. We describe the case of a 16-year-old girl with restrictive AN who experienced a severe clinical relapse requiring hospitalization after a previously disclosed but unprocessed experience of childhood sexual abuse was revisited in greater detail during routine outpatient psychotherapy for AN. Although the psychotherapy was not trauma-focused, it aimed to reconstruct the patient's developmental history and identify the maintaining mechanisms of the eating disorder within a specialist multidisciplinary eating-disorder service. Revisiting the traumatic experience was followed by marked emotional distress and a severe exacerbation of restrictive symptoms. This case highlights the complex relationship between trauma and AN during adolescence and underscores the clinical importance of carefully assessing emotional regulation capacities and medical stability when traumatic experiences are revisited in severely vulnerable patients. A phase-based, trauma-informed multidisciplinary approach may be particularly important for adolescents whose restrictive symptoms continue to function as primary defensive and affect-regulatory mechanisms.

items.title: Effects of different doses of esketamine as an adjunct to sufentanil-based patient-controlled intravenous analgesia on postoperative analgesia and opioid consumption following lumbar decompression surgery: a dose-finding randomized controlled trial.
items.authors: Liu JJ, Wang X, Ding PP, Wang HJ, Zhang TT, Hu XW.

sections.text: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of different doses of esketamine as an adjunct to sufentanil-based patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) on postoperative analgesia and opioid consumption after lumbar decompression surgery and to explore its optimal risk-benefit dose. A total of 120 patients scheduled for lumbar decompression surgery were randomly allocated to four groups. The control group (Group N, n = 30) received PCIA with sufentanil 2.5 μg/kg. To test the opioid-sparing hypothesis, the three experimental groups (Groups S1, S2, and S3, n = 30 each) received PCIA with a lower sufentanil dose (1.5 μg/kg) combined with esketamine at 0.25, 0.5, and 1.0 mg/kg, respectively. All PCIA solutions were diluted with normal saline to a total volume of 100 mL. The primary outcome was the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain score at rest. Secondary outcomes included sufentanil consumption, PCIA press counts, requirement for rescue analgesia, Ramsay Sedation Scale (RSS) scores, and oxidative-stress markers; safety endpoints were analyzed as exploratory outcomes. Postoperative adverse effects, including nausea, vomiting, dizziness, respiratory depression, hypotension, and psychiatric symptoms (dissociation or nightmares), were recorded and compared across the four groups. All esketamine-containing regimens (S1-S3) showed significantly lower VAS scores at all postoperative time points compared with Group N (P < 0.05), with no statistically significant difference among S1, S2, and S3. The 24-h sufentanil consumption, effective PCIA presses, and rescue analgesia demand were also significantly reduced (P < 0.05). However, Ramsay sedation scores increased dose-dependently (S3 > S2 > S1). At 4 h postoperatively, SOD activity was higher, and concentrations of MDA, GLU, and COR were lower in all esketamine-containing regimens compared with Group N. Although the overall incidence of adverse events was comparable, the high-dose group (S3) had a significantly increased incidence of hypotension and dissociative symptoms. Adding esketamine to a reduced-sufentanil PCIA regimen improved postoperative analgesia and reduced opioid consumption after lumbar decompression surgery. Analgesic benefit was similar across the tested doses (0.25-1.0 mg/kg), whereas dose-related adverse effects (sedation, hypotension, psychomimetic symptoms) increased with dose. These findings suggest that 0.25 mg/kg may provide a favorable efficacy-safety balance within the investigated dose range. http://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.aspx?proj=249890, Identifier: ChiCTR2500095890.

items.title: Decomposition and comparative analysis of the differences in anxiety symptoms in preschool children with only and non-only children: a cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Xie Y, Wang W, Tuersun Y, Yin X, Zhou Q, Liang Z, Peng S, Li X, Huang J.

sections.text: Against the backdrop of family structure transformation and increasing attention to child mental health, anxiety symptoms in preschool children have become an important public health issue. Anxiety symptoms not only affect early emotional regulation and social adaptation but may also have sustained impacts on subsequent psychological development. In the context of China's unique population policy, significant differences exist between only children and non-only children in terms of family resource allocation, parent-child interactions, and developmental environment, which may further influence the manifestation of childhood anxiety symptoms. This study aims to compare the differences in the detection rates of anxiety symptoms between only-child and non-only-child preschool children, identify the differential effects of individual, family, and neurobehavioral factors on the two groups, and quantify the contributions of various factors to between-group differences using the Fairlie decomposition model, thereby providing empirical evidence for targeted child mental health intervention strategies. This cross-sectional study was based on data from the 2022 Longhua Child Cohort Study in Shenzhen, China. A total of 67,779 preschool children aged 3-6 years (46,565 only children; 21,214 non-only children) were included and divided into two groups according to only-child status. Anxiety symptoms were assessed using the Chinese version of the Spence Preschool Anxiety Scale (SPAS, cutoff ≥48). Sociodemographic characteristics, ADHD symptoms, and emotional and behavioral problems were also collected. Chi-square tests and multivariate logistic regression were used to analyze associated factors, and the Fairlie decomposition model was applied to decompose between-group differences and quantify the contribution of each factor to the disparity in anxiety symptoms. The overall detection rate of anxiety symptoms in preschool children was 3.48%, with only-children showing a slightly higher rate (3.6%) than non-only children (3.3%, P = 0.027). Although the difference reached statistical significance, the absolute magnitude of the difference was small. Multivariate logistic regression revealed that higher maternal education level (OR = 0.710-0.751) and higher household income (OR = 0.426-0.623) were both associated with a decreased risk of anxiety symptoms. In contrast, female sex (OR = 1.224-1.276), positive ADHD symptoms (OR≈2.53), and abnormal SDQ total difficulties scores (OR≈18.28) were associated with an increased risk of anxiety, serving as risk factors for anxiety symptoms. Fairlie decomposition results showed that 39.8% of the total difference in anxiety symptoms between the two groups could be explained by observed variables, with emotional and behavioral problems contributing the most (41.43%), followed by ADHD symptoms (17.93%) and gender (3.42%). Meanwhile, maternal education level and household income exhibited significant negative contributions (-19.67%and-5.91%, respectively), suggesting that higher socioeconomic status served as a "protective buffer" against anxiety risk for only children. The remaining 60.2% of the difference may be attributable to unobserved factors. There was a statistically significant difference in the detection rate of anxiety symptoms between only-child and non-only-child preschool children. This disparity was influenced by multiple factors, including children's emotional and behavioral problems, ADHD symptoms, and family socioeconomic factors. However, the practical significance of this difference still requires further interpretation in conjunction with additional family environmental variables. In light of the differing mental health needs of children from diverse family structures, this study recommends establishing a mental health monitoring system centered on SDQ screening, implementing differentiated family education guidance tailored to different family structures, and promoting a collaborative mental health support system involving kindergartens, families, and communities.

items.title: Longitudinal associations between childhood maltreatment and suicidal ideation in youth: the roles of complex posttraumatic stress disorder symptoms and interpersonal factors.
items.authors: Yu Q, Li Y, Wang L, Guo J, Wang W.

sections.text: Globally, suicide ranks as the third leading cause of death among youth, with risk particularly pronounced among those who have experienced childhood maltreatment. Guided by the developmental model of suicide risk and the interpersonal theory of suicide, this study aimed to examine the link between childhood maltreatment and suicidal ideation in youth, and to investigate the mediating roles of complex posttraumatic stress disorder (CPTSD) symptoms and interpersonal needs. Three-wave longitudinal data from 1,427 college students (53.7% female) with childhood maltreatment were included. Participants completed self-report measures assessing childhood maltreatment, CPTSD symptoms, perceived burdensomeness (PB) and thwarted belongingness (TB), and suicidal ideation. Structural equation modeling was conducted to evaluate the proposed pathways. Findings indicated that PB, rather than TB, functions as the primary proximal risk factor for suicidal ideation. Furthermore, within CPTSD, disturbances in self-organization (DSO), rather than posttraumatic stress (PTS), mediated the association between childhood maltreatment and PB. Specifically, childhood maltreatment was indirectly associated with PB through the negative self-concept dimension of DSO, and PB was subsequently positively associated with suicidal ideation. These findings suggest that, for youth with childhood maltreatment, DSO may be even more critical than PTS in understanding suicidal ideation. Intervention strategies targeting negative self-concept may be particularly effective in reducing suicidal ideation among youth.

items.title: Longitudinal relationships between anxiety and fear of progression in post-CABG patients: a cross-sectional and cross-lagged panel network analysis.
items.authors: Luo Z, Chen F, Li H, Wang W, Chen D, Guo Y, Xing J, Liang F, Tao J.

sections.text: Patients following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) frequently experience elevated anxiety and fear of progression (FoP), which has a high comorbidity and significantly increases adverse postoperative event risks. This prospective study explored the dynamic longitudinal associations between anxiety and FoP in post-CABG patients using network analysis methods. A prospective longitudinal design enrolled first-time CABG patients from three tertiary hospitals in Urumqi, China. Anxiety and FoP were assessed using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) and the Fear of Progression Questionnaire-Short Form (FoP-Q-SF) at three time points: hospital discharge (T1), 1 month (T2), and 3 months (T3) post-discharge. Cross-sectional Gaussian Graphical Models were constructed at each time point, and cross-lagged panel network (CLPN) analysis was performed to examine longitudinal symptom associations. Six a priori selected covariates (age, gender, educational level, duration of CHD, chronic comorbidities, and NYHA functional classification) were residualized prior to network estimation. A total of 343 patients were included in the network analysis. From T1 to T3, total GAD-7 scores demonstrated a notable downward trend, whereas FoP-Q-SF scores exhibited a continuous upward trend. The core node at both T1 and T2 was FoP11 "Worrying about what will become of the family if something should happen to the patient, " which shifted to FoP2 "Being nervous prior to doctors' appointments or periodic examinations" at T3. items.title: Network analysis of trauma-related mental health comorbidities under continuous traumatic stress: a comparative study of South African and Ukrainian adolescents.
items.authors: Zasiekina L, van der Watt ASJ, Holland M, Solonenko O, Seedat S.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Adolescents living under conditions of continuous traumatic stress (CTS) are exposed to ongoing, persistent, unpredictable threats that differ from past discrete traumatic events and are associated with high levels of CTS symptoms, posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), depression, and anxiety. Despite growing evidence that CTS functions as a risk factor for trauma-related disorders, little is known about how specific CTS symptoms are embedded within broader psychopathology networks across diverse contexts of chronic violence.

sections.heading: Aim
sections.text: This study applied item-level network analysis to examine the structural role of individual CTS symptoms within PTSD, depression, and anxiety symptom networks among adolescents exposed to CTS in South Africa ( n  = 600) and Ukraine ( n  = 485).

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: Adolescents (aged 12 to 18 years) completed standardised measures of CTS, PTSD, depression, and anxiety symptoms. Item-level network models were used to examine within- and cross-domain symptom associations, identify central and bridging CTS symptoms, assess their predictive value for overall symptom severity, and test network invariance across countries.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: In both samples, strong within-domain clustering was observed alongside robust cross-domain connections linking CTS symptoms with PTSD, depression, and anxiety symptoms. In Ukraine, CTS symptoms were represented by symptoms reflecting loss of meaning, intense fear or horror, and episodes of rage, while in South Africa, CTS symptoms were represented by difficulty controlling emotions, feelings of betrayal, and perceived life threat. The findings also suggest that CTS symptoms were more tightly interconnected and more evenly distributed across PTSD, depression, and anxiety symptoms in the Ukrainian sample, whereas the South African sample demonstrated a broader and more diffuse symptom pattern, with anxiety-related symptoms appearing to be more prominently expressed.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Findings suggest that CTS symptoms may potentially operate as a transdiagnostic process - cutting across, and contributing to shared variance in PTSD, depression, and anxiety symptoms - among adolescents exposed to ongoing violence. Interventions targeting core CTS bridge symptoms may reduce comorbidity and improve mental health outcomes in chronically threatened youth across diverse conflict settings.

items.title: Neuroprogression of chronic stress-induced depression via longitudinal fMRI.
items.authors: Yang Y, Jia H, Liu H.

sections.text: Depression is increasingly viewed as a progressive neurobiological trajectory, yet the spatiotemporal transition from early mood dysregulation to chronic network failure, and its relation to disease-related functional decline, remains unclear. Using a chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mouse model, we aimed to map the longitudinal brain transformation from local spontaneous activity to global network dysfunction via multi-parametric MRI. Longitudinal functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) was performed on a cohort of CUMS mice (n = 7) across three longitudinal time points: Day 0 (baseline), Day 5 CUMS, and Day 10 CUMS. We integrated four analytical approaches: fALFF, static functional connectivity, graph theory, and dFC/dALFF. Depression progression followed a hierarchical spatiotemporal dissolution. fALFF revealed sequential breakdown of local hubs in caudoputamen, medial prefrontal cortex, and hippocampus, suggesting involvement of motor-motivational and executive deficits. sFC showed sensory-limbic uncoupling between caudoputamen and visual areas, and altered mPFC-AON connectivity and hippocampal prefrontal (HPF-PL) dysconnectivity, indicating limbic-olfactory loop disruption. Graph theory indicated preserved global node efficiency but widespread loss of node local efficiency and clustering. Dynamic analyses uncovered a shift from flexible network reconfiguration to dynamic rigidity. Longitudinal CUMS exposure was associated with progressive alterations in functional network organization. The prefrontal olfactory dysconnectivity and onset of dynamic rigidity represent candidate multi-scale and longitudinal imaging features that warrant future validation.

items.title: Animation-assisted psychological intervention in pediatric care: mechanisms, clinical applications, and emerging evidence.
items.authors: Dongxian W, Zeqi Y, Qi S, Shutong W.

sections.text: Children frequently experience fear, anxiety, and pain during medical encounters, and this distress can lead to poor cooperation, longer procedures, and lasting avoidance of care. Animation, delivered as cartoons, preparation films, applications, serious games, and virtual reality (VR) scenes, has become one of the most widely deployed non-pharmacological adjuncts in pediatric settings because it is inexpensive, non-invasive, and easily standardized. Drawing on a structured search of six databases through July 2026, this mini-review synthesizes randomized and meta-analytic evidence across perioperative anxiety, procedural pain, pediatric dentistry, chronic-disease self-management, and mental health promotion. It organizes the evidence around five psychological pathways: attentional competition, observational learning, exposure and inhibitory learning, narrative-affective processing, and self-efficacy. Additionally, it examines a sixth, non-psychological use in which animation is used to provide therapeutic visual stimulation. Evidence supports moderate short-term benefits for anticipatory anxiety and for needle- and dentistry-related distress, with weaker and less consistent effects for high-intensity procedures and physiological outcomes. We argue that the field's core issue is conceptual rather than empirical: animation refers to a delivery medium, not a treatment, and trials have compared media rather than mechanisms. This obscures three unresolved problems: discordance between self-reported and autonomic outcomes; an untheorized moderating role of the developmental stage; and a theoretical tension between distraction, which withdraws attention from the feared stimulus, and exposure, which requires engagement with it. Mechanism-matched comparators, core outcome sets, developmentally stratified designs, transparent intervention reporting, and follow-up across repeated procedures are prerequisites for cumulative progress.

items.title: Intimate partner violence and depressive symptoms among ever-partnered Peruvian women: a repeated cross-sectional analysis of national surveys, 2015-2024.
items.authors: Arce-Huamani MA, Picon-Flores LR, Fuentes-Cosme FF, Benites-Pereda MX, de Souza DLB, De la Cruz-Ku G, Ortiz-Arica MM, Torres-Roman JS, Tasayco-Marquez LM.

sections.text: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a major public health concern associated with adverse mental health outcomes in women. We examined trends in depressive symptoms and temporal variation in their association with IPV among ever-partnered Peruvian women from 2015 to 2024. We conducted a repeated cross-sectional analysis using data from 10 consecutive national ENDES surveys. The primary weighted analytic sample included 101,145 women aged 15-49 years. Depressive symptoms were defined as a PHQ-9 score ≥10. Survey-weighted prevalence ratios were estimated using modified Poisson regression with robust variance. Overall, 35.3% of women reported any IPV, including physical (28.0%), emotional (24.5%), and sexual IPV (6.1%). The weighted prevalence of depressive symptoms was 7.1%. The estimated annual relative change was +2.31% (95% CI: 1.03-3.61%; p < 0.001), with a non-monotonic annual pattern. Any IPV was associated with higher prevalence of depressive symptoms (aPR: 2.37; 95% CI: 2.18-2.58). Emotional, physical, and sexual IPV were also associated with depressive symptoms (aPRs: 2.32 [95% CI: 2.14-2.53], 2.21 [95% CI: 2.04-2.39], and 1.97 [95% CI: 1.80-2.17], respectively). The association varied across periods: 2015-2019, aPR 2.72; 2020-2021, 1.77; and 2022-2024, 2.29 (p for interaction <0.001). IPV was consistently associated with depressive symptoms, although the magnitude varied over time. These findings support integrated, confidential identification of IPV alongside timely mental health assessment and referral, without establishing the effectiveness of any specific screening strategy.

items.title: Mental health, academic performance, and addictive behaviors among university student carers.
items.authors: Landi G, Pakenham KI, Ambrosini F, Bao Z, Tossani E, Grandi S.

sections.text: Student mental health is an emerging global public health priority in higher education. Preliminary evidence indicates that caregiving is a mental health risk factor in university students. This study investigates demographic, educational, and caregiving variables as potential risk factors for university student carer mental health (anxiety, depression), addictive behaviors, and academic performance problems. 2,533 university students in Italy completed an online cross-sectional survey assessing depressive symptoms (Patient Health Questionnaire-9), anxiety symptoms (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7), 10 addictive behaviors (Screener for Substance and Behavioral Addictions), and self-assessed academic performance. Predictors included demographics variables (sex, age, nationality), educational variables (degree programme, residential status, enrollment status), caregiving context variables (carer-care recipient relationship, care recipient's type of health condition) and caregiving responsibilities. Student carers living with a family member with a serious health condition comprised 30.1% of the sample (n = 762). Compared with non-carers, carers reported higher depressive symptoms (B = 1.83, 95% CI [1.33, 2.33]; β = 0.14), higher anxiety symptoms (B = 1.32, 95% CI [0.87, 1.77]; β = 0.11), and lower academic performance (B = -0.21, 95% CI [-0.39, -0.02]; β = -0.05). Carer status was also associated with higher odds of problematic involvement in cannabis (OR = 1.69, 95% CI [1.25, 2.28]), food consumption (OR = 1.62, 95% CI [1.34, 1.95]), shopping (OR = 1.39, 95% CI [1.09, 1.78]), videogaming (OR = 1.29, 95% CI [1.06, 1.57]), and social-network use (OR = 1.26, 95% CI [1.06, 1.50]). Within the student-carer subgroup, after adjusting for all demographic, educational, caregiving-context, and caregiving-responsibility variables, caring for a family member with a mental health condition or intellectual disability was associated with higher depressive symptoms (B = 1.66, 95% CI [0.54, 2.79]). Greater caregiving responsibilities were associated with higher depressive symptoms (B = 1.12, 95% CI [0.62, 1.62]), higher anxiety symptoms (B = 1.01, 95% CI [0.57, 1.44]), and higher odds of problematic food consumption (OR = 1.32, 95% CI [1.10, 1.59]), and physical exercise (OR = 1.31, 95% CI [1.08, 1.59]). Findings replicate prior evidence showing student carers are at higher risk than non-carer peers for mental health problems. Results extend prior research showing student carers are also at higher risk for addictive behaviors and poorer self-assessed academic performance. Findings highlight the incremental and simultaneous contributions of demographic, educational, and caregiving variables as risk factors for student carer mental health and addictive behaviors.
