items.title: Sport participation and gambling-related problems in adolescents: findings from a large school-based study.
items.authors: Ratković D, Knežević V, Dickov A, Ivanović-Kovačević S, Savić P, Ivetić O, Bjelan S, Čomić M.

sections.text: Adolescent gambling is increasingly shaped by digital access, sports betting, and gambling-like mechanisms embedded in everyday youth culture. This study examined gambling-related problems among high school students and their associations with sociodemographic, family, mental health-related, and behavioral characteristics, with particular attention to sport participation. A school-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 2,379 high school students in Novi Sad, Serbia, between 2024 and 2026. Participants completed a structured sociodemographic and behavioral questionnaire and the Serbian version of the Gambling Disorder Identification Test. Students were classified as non-gambling, recreational gambling, or having gambling-related problems. Associations between gambling categories and selected characteristics were examined using omnibus chi-square tests, Cramér's V, and post-hoc pairwise comparisons. Overall, 1,969 students (82.8%) were classified as non-gambling, 314 (13.2%) as recreational gambling, and 96 (4.0%) as having gambling-related problems. Gambling category was significantly associated with male sex, lower school achievement, living arrangement, parental marital status, sport participation, previous psychiatric treatment, family psychiatric history, smoking, alcohol use, and psychoactive substance use. In the univariate analyses, sport participation increased from 64.0% among non-gambling students to 75.2% among recreational gamblers and 78.1% among students with gambling-related problems. Post-hoc comparisons showed that sport participation differentiated non-gambling students from both gambling-involved groups, but not recreational gambling from gambling-related problems. However, after adjustment for sex and other relevant behavioral and mental health-related characteristics, sport participation was no longer independently associated with gambling-related problems. Male sex, previous psychiatric treatment, smoking, alcohol use, and psychoactive substance use remained the strongest independent correlates. Gambling-related problems in adolescents were associated with a broader pattern of behavioral and mental health-related factors. Although sport participation was associated with gambling involvement in unadjusted analyses, this association did not remain significant after adjustment for sex and other relevant characteristics. These findings support understanding adolescent gambling within a broader risk-behavior and public health framework, with sport representing a relevant context for prevention rather than an independent risk factor.

items.title: The Association Between Prenatal Anxiety and Depression and Autism Spectrum Disorder With Gastrointestinal Symptoms in Children: Case-Control Study.
items.authors: Cheng B, Wan E, He Y, Wang S, He Y, Lyu X.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Studies have indicated that maternal anxiety and depression during pregnancy can contribute to neurodevelopmental disorders and gut flora dysbiosis in children. However, it is unclear whether these factors increase the risk of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) with gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms in children.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aimed to analyze the relationship between maternal anxiety and depression during pregnancy and ASD with GI symptoms.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A total of 470 children with ASD and 486 children with typical development were enrolled in the study. The caregivers of all enrolled children completed questionnaires, including information on maternal mental health and GI symptoms.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The percentage of maternal prenatal anxiety or depression was significantly higher in the ASD group than in the typical development group ( P <.001). Children whose mothers experienced anxiety or depression during pregnancy had substantially higher risk of developing ASD than those whose mothers did not experience these conditions (unadjusted odds ratio [OR] 4.274, 95% CI 2.799-6.526; adjusted OR 3.897, 95% CI 2.481-6.119). For children with ASD, those whose mothers had prenatal anxiety or depression had a significantly higher risk of GI symptoms than those whose mothers did not have these conditions (unadjusted OR 1.883, 95% CI 1.209-2.934; adjusted OR 1.943, 95% CI 1.236-3.054).

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Mothers who experience anxiety or depression during pregnancy may have a higher likelihood of their children developing ASD with GI symptoms.

items.title: Panax ginseng in psychiatric disorders: Mechanisms and therapeutic potentials.
items.authors: Choi HJ, Choe YM, Kim JH, Suh GH, Lee BC, Hwang J, Kim SG, Kim HS, Yi D, Kim JW.

sections.text: Panax ginseng C.A. Meyer is a traditional medicinal herb with a long-standing history as a tonic and adaptogen. Accumulating evidence suggests its therapeutic potential for enhancing mood and cognition, as well as mitigating stress-related psychiatric conditions. This comprehensive review assesses the neuropharmacological mechanisms and potential therapeutic effects of Panax ginseng in psychiatric disorders, based on preclinical and clinical data. Ginseng and its active constituents, particularly ginsenosides, modulate key neurotransmitter systems-including serotonin, dopamine, norepinephrine, and gamma-aminobutyric acid-while exerting neuroprotective, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant effects. Furthermore, it plays a crucial role in regulating the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis and stress responses. Preclinical models have shown antidepressant and anxiolytic properties comparable to conventional pharmacotherapies, alongside pro-cognitive and neuroprotective actions. Although clinical evidence remains emerging, existing studies indicate potential benefits for depression, anxiety, and cognitive impairment, specifically improving symptoms in patients with Alzheimer's disease and schizophrenia. Consequently, Panax ginseng may hold promise as an adjunctive therapy for various psychiatric disorders. Its multimodal mechanisms-encompassing monoamine modulation, neurotrophic support, and adaptogenic stress reduction-provide a rationale for its clinical application. Nonetheless, rigorous large-scale clinical trials are essential to confirm efficacy, determine optimal dosing, and ensure safety.

items.title: Exploring the association between bullying and depression symptoms among adolescents in Bangladesh: Findings from nationally representative survey.
items.authors: Amin R, Asgar ASMR.

sections.text: Bullying victimization is an important public health concern that has been linked to adverse psychological outcomes among adolescents. The study used mental health well-being data collected in the most recent Bangladesh Adolescent Health and Wellbeing Survey (2019-2020) (BAHWS). A total of 9,116 adolescents aged 15-19 years with complete depression data were included in the analysis. A three-level linear mixed-effects model was employed to account for the hierarchical structure of the survey, with adolescents nested within primary sampling units and districts. Additional analyses examined gender and marital status interactions, subgroup differences, and the cumulative association between multiple forms of bullying and depressive symptoms using a composite bullying measure. The findings revealed that verbal bullying (β = 1.39, p < 0.001) and cyberbullying (β = 1.15, p = 0.012) were independently associated with higher depressive symptom scores. The association between physical bullying and depressive symptoms differed significantly by gender, whereas interactions of gender with verbal and cyberbullying were not statistically significant. Exploratory subgroup analyses showed variation in the magnitude of estimated associations across ever-married females, unmarried females, and unmarried males. A graded association was observed for cumulative bullying exposure: compared with adolescents reporting no bullying exposure, those exposed to on (β = 1.25), two (β = 2.61), and three (β = 4.99) bullying types had progressively higher depressive symptom scores (all p < 0.001). Adolescent Age, Current school or college attendance and higher household wealth were associated with lower depressive symptom scores. Bullying victimization, particularly verbal bullying, cyberbullying, and exposure to multiple forms of bullying, was associated with higher depressive symptoms among Bangladeshi adolescents. These findings highlight the need for comprehensive bullying prevention strategies and accessible psychosocial support services, with particular attention to adolescents experiencing multiple forms of bullying and other vulnerable groups.

items.title: Implementing Routine Mental Health Screening and Structured Follow-up for Youth With Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis: A Single-center Quality Improvement Project.
items.authors: Xiao E, Beattie K, Cellucci T, Dushnicky M, Heale L, Herrington J, Prowse K, Batthish M.

sections.text: Youth with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) have higher rates of anxiety and depression, yet pediatric rheumatology clinics rarely embed systematic mental health care into routine care. Unrecognized symptoms can impair physical functioning and disease management. The objectives of this quality improvement initiative were to increase (1) anxiety/depression screening from 0% to ≥75% and (2) algorithm-concordant follow-up for youth screening positive from 0% to ≥75%. Our team implemented iterative plan-do-study-act cycles in a pediatric rheumatology clinic at McMaster Children's Hospital. A key driver diagram and fishbone analysis informed interventions, including workflow redesign, staff training, electronic medical record supports, and a standardized follow-up algorithm. We screened youth with JIA 12-18 years of age using the Patient Health Questionnaire-4 (PHQ-4), an ultra-brief self-report tool used to detect anxiety and depression. Process measures included the percentage of eligible visits with PHQ-4 screening completed and the percentage of screened visits with documented algorithm-concordant follow-up. Outcome measures captured screening results while balancing measures assessed patient and healthcare provider acceptability. PHQ-4 screening increased from 0% to sustained percentages of ≥75% across 266 audited visits (May 2024-August 2025). Overall, 17% of youth screened positive (PHQ-4 ≥ 3). After implementing the follow-up algorithm, ≥75% of screened visits documented education, referral, and/or safety planning. Screening was acceptable to patients and health care providers, with no reported workflow disruption. Embedding PHQ-4 screening with a structured follow-up pathway is feasible and sustainable in a pediatric rheumatology clinic, supporting timely and equitable identification of mental health needs and advancing integrated biopsychosocial care for youth with JIA.

items.title: Antipsychotic Prescriptions for Prenatal and Postpartum Women in Japan: A Large Claims Database Study.
items.authors: Obara R, Sakai T, Ishikawa T, Morishita K, Adomi M, Hara A, Kikuchi S, Kobayashi N, Iwama N, Shinoda G, Noda A, Orui M, Ishikuro M, Tomita H, Mano N, Kuriyama S, Obara T.

sections.text: This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of antipsychotic prescriptions before, during, and after pregnancy in Japan, with a focus on new prescriptions and continuation after pregnancy confirmation. We conducted a claims-based analysis using a Japanese claims database (analytic period: 2010-2022). Antipsychotic prescription prevalence and new prescriptions were assessed from 180 days before pregnancy through 180 days postpartum. To assess continuation after pregnancy confirmation, prescription status was evaluated across gestational weeks 0-4, 5-13, and from 14 weeks to delivery. Among 120 735 women, 1698 (140.6/10 000 deliveries) received at least one antipsychotic prescription, including 809 (67.0/10 000 deliveries) during pregnancy. Prescription prevalence decreased during the first and second trimesters but increased postpartum. New prescriptions were less frequent during pregnancy but increased after delivery. Among 611 women prescribed antipsychotics during 0-4 weeks' gestation, 482 (78.9%) continued and 129 (21.1%) discontinued prescription during weeks 5-13; of those who continued prescription during 5-13 weeks, 334 (54.7%) continued until delivery. Evaluation of major indications showed that continuation until delivery was highest in those with schizophrenia (63.6%), followed by bipolar disorder (51.0%). This study provides the first comprehensive description of perinatal antipsychotic prescription trends in Japan. Substantial prescription discontinuation occurred after pregnancy confirmation. Increases in postpartum prescriptions might reflect new prescriptions or resumption among women who had discontinued treatment during pregnancy. These findings offer foundational epidemiological insights into real-world perinatal antipsychotic use.

items.title: Fecal Microbiota Transplantation: A Promising Therapeutic Strategy Targeting the Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis in Anorexia Nervosa.
items.authors: Kwok SL, Xiao YC, Cai XB.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a complex psychiatric disorder characterized by self-starvation, body-image disturbance, and serious medical complications. Because current treatments have variable outcomes and relapse is common, the microbiota-gut-brain axis has been investigated as a possible contributor to disease persistence. This review evaluates fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) as an experimental microbiota-directed strategy for AN.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for relevant studies published from January 1990 to October 2025. Eligible evidence included human reports, animal studies, and mechanistic studies examining FMT or gut-microbiota alterations in AN and related pathways.

sections.heading: Findings
sections.text: Individuals with AN have been reported to show altered microbial diversity and changes in taxa associated with short-chain fatty acid production and inflammation. These findings are heterogeneous and may reflect starvation, diet, medication exposure, or illness-related physiology. Human evidence for FMT in AN is limited to small, uncontrolled studies and case reports, while most mechanistic support comes from animal models or indirect evidence from other conditions.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Evidence for FMT in AN remains preliminary and is largely based on uncontrolled human observations and preclinical studies. FMT may alter gut microbial composition and gastrointestinal or metabolic measures, but controlled efficacy data are absent and psychiatric benefits remain unconfirmed. Well-designed controlled trials are needed to establish its safety and clinical efficacy.

items.title: Mediterranean diet adherence, social media use, and anxiety symptoms: an exploratory cross-sectional pilot survey.
items.authors: Religa P, Mickael ME, Kubick N, Conesa Moreno I, Ferris Garcia D, Sacharczuk M, Atanasov AG, Horbańczuk JO.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Anxiety and depressive symptoms are common, and dietary patterns have been proposed as a modifiable influence on them. The majority of the evidence rests on composite adherence indices such as the Mediterranean Diet Adherence Screener (MEDAS), which sums its components as if they all contributed equally and addresses depression more often than anxiety. Whether individual dietary components relate to symptoms independently of the composite index has rarely been tested, and rarely alongside social media use, a further exposure proposed to shape both diet and mood.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: An anonymous online survey in English, Spanish, and Russian was completed by 115 adults aged 18 to 65 years with no previous diagnosis of mental illness, comprising a 14-item modified Mediterranean Diet Score (mMEDS), the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), and questions on daily time spent on Instagram, Facebook, and Twitter/X. Four primary hypotheses tested the associations of olive oil intake and red and processed meat intake with each HADS subscale; all other comparisons were exploratory. The Benjamini-Hochberg correction was applied within each family. Effect sizes are reported with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. The primary comparisons were additionally adjusted for sex, age band, and educational level.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: All four primary estimates lay in the hypothesized direction. Higher olive oil intake was associated with lower anxiety scores ( r  = -0.249, 95% CI - 0.448 to -0.050, p  = 0.021), and restricted red and processed meat intake was associated with lower anxiety and depression scores after adjustment ( β  = -2.12, p  = 0.021; β  = -1.62, p  = 0.032). None survived correction for multiple testing. The mMEDS total did not appear to be related to either subscale ( ρ  = -0.045 and -0.141), while item-level associations differed in direction across food groups.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Component-level signals appeared where the composite showed none, which may indicate that summing adherence items can obscure relationships running in opposite directions between foods. For studies using MEDAS-type indices, testing components alongside the total score could be worthwhile. Olive oil quantity and red and processed meat intake may be candidates for confirmatory work.

items.title: Adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomal miR-22-3p alleviates depression-like behaviors in a rat model via the FURIN/HMGB1 axis.
items.authors: Xu Y, You Y, Wei D, Liang R, Liang W, Feng B, Chen J, Liang J, Li F.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is characterized by neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis, yet effective brain-targeted delivery strategies remain limited. Exosomes represent promising carriers capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier. This study investigated whether engineered exosomes delivering miR-22-3p by modulating the FURIN/HMGB1 axis.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Serum microRNA expression was assessed in patients with MDD. A rat model of depression was established using chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS). miR-22-3p-engineered adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell exosomes were administered intranasally. Behavioral tests (SPT, OFT, FST), RT-qPCR, ELISA, HE staining, and TUNEL assays were performed to evaluate neurobehavioral and molecular changes.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: miR-22-3p was significantly downregulated in both MDD patients and CUMS rats (P < 0.01). Intranasal administration of engineered exosomes increased brain miR-22-3p levels and significantly improved depressive-like behaviors (P < 0.05 or P < 0.01). Mechanistically, treatment suppressed FURIN and HMGB1 expression, reduced proinflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α), and attenuated hippocampal neuronal apoptosis (P < 0.05 or P < 0.01). These effects were more pronounced than those of native exosomes.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: miR-22-3p-engineered exosomes exert antidepressant effects by inhibiting the FURIN/HMGB1-mediated neuroinflammatory and apoptotic pathways. This study highlights a novel intranasal exosome-based microRNA delivery strategy for MDD.

items.title: Resistance training volume for major depressive disorder: the MoveMind randomized controlled trial protocol.
items.authors: Quizzini GH, Campos JMS, Amorim TAM, Dos Santos MAA, da Cruz AFO, Jokura MS, Correia MAM, Baraldo JE, Trombetta-Lima M, Nascimento C, Deslandes A, Werneck AO, Stubbs B, Islam H, Jiménez-Maldonado A, Schuch FB, Neves LM, Rossi FE.

sections.text: This randomized controlled trial aims to investigate the effects of resistance training (RT) volume (high vs. low) and non-exercise group on depressive symptoms, remission rates, adherence and the psychological and neurobiological mechanisms underlying these effects in patients with major depressive disorder (MDD). A total of 150 adults (18-59 years) diagnosed with MDD will be randomized into three groups: high-volume RT (HV, n=50; 4 sets of 10-12 repetition maximum [RM]), low-volume RT (LV, n=50; 2 sets of 10-12 RM), and a non-exercise control group (CG, n=50). Participants in the intervention groups will train three non-consecutive days per week for 8 weeks. The primary outcome, depressive symptoms, will be assessed by a psychiatrist using the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale. Secondary outcomes will include potential psychological mechanisms (perceived self-efficacy, affective responses to exercise, and well-being), assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and at the 3-month follow-up, and neurobiological mechanisms assessed by inflammatory and metabolic biomarkers related to MDD pathophysiology, including TNF-α, IL-6, IL-10, IL-1β, CRP, IGF-1, BDNF, insulin, glucose, and cortisol, measured before and after the intervention. Tertiary outcomes will include dietary intake and ultra-processed food consumption (24-hour dietary recall), body composition (DXA), muscular strength, and sleep quality. Intervention efficacy will be analyzed using intention-to-treat linear mixed-effects models. The findings may contribute to more effective, personalized, and sustainable RT prescriptions that improve adherence and complement conventional treatments for MDD.

items.title: Emotional regulation ability and depressive symptoms among Chinese junior high school students: a cross-sectional analysis of the role of stress coping styles.
items.authors: Wang J, Yang L, Guo R, Liu D, Li M.

sections.text: While emotional regulation and coping styles influence adolescent depression, the mediating role of coping styles in the link between emotional regulation ability and depressive symptoms remains underexplored among junior high school students-a critical developmental stage marked by immature coping patterns. This study explores the correlations among emotional regulation ability, stress coping styles (problem-focused and emotion-focused coping), and depressive symptoms among junior high school students and examines the mediating effect of stress coping styles on the relationship between emotional regulation ability and depressive symptoms. A total of 600 junior high school students were recruited between September and December 2024 through a multi-school convenience sampling approach involving five junior high schools across three cities in Henan Province. A self-designed general information questionnaire, the Patient Health Questionnaire Depression Scale (PHQ-9), the Adolescent Coping Style Scale and the Emotional Regulation Ability Questionnaire were used in the investigation. Pearson correlation analysis was used to examine the associations among problem-focused coping, emotion-focused coping, emotional regulation ability, and depressive symptoms, and a cross-sectional indirect association analysis was conducted to examine whether the two coping styles statistically accounted for indirect associations between emotional regulation ability and depressive symptoms. Among the 471 valid responses received, emotional regulation ability was significantly negatively associated with depressive symptoms (r = -0.523, P < 0.001). In the parallel mediation analysis, emotional regulation ability was significantly associated with problem-focused coping (B = -0.0733, P = 0.023) and was directly and negatively associated with depressive symptoms (B = -0.1283, P < 0.001), but was not significantly associated with emotion-focused coping (B = -0.0465, P = 0.067). The total indirect effect was not significant (effect = -0.0002, 95% CI: -0.0038-0.0033]), thus indicating that neither coping style significantly mediated this association. This study demonstrated that emotional regulation ability is significantly and negatively associated with depressive symptoms among junior high school students. However, neither problem-focused coping nor emotion-focused coping significantly mediate the relationship between emotional regulation ability and depressive symptoms. These findings indicate that greater emotional regulation ability is associated with fewer depressive symptoms in early adolescence, whereas stress coping styles may not function as stable mediators at this developmental stage. These results support prioritizing the evaluation of developmentally appropriate emotional regulation programs for junior high school students in school and community settings.

Pearson correlation analysis was used to examine the associations among problem-focused coping, emotion-focused coping, emotional regulation ability, and depressive symptoms, and a cross-sectional indirect association analysis was conducted to examine whether the two coping styles statistically accounted for indirect associations between emotional regulation ability and depressive symptoms. The total indirect effect was not significant (effect = -0.0002, 95% CI: -0.0038-0.0033]), thus indicating that neither coping style significantly mediated this association. This study demonstrated that emotional regulation ability is significantly and negatively associated with depressive symptoms among junior high school students. items.title: Which classroom anxiety experience should teachers target first? A network-simulation study of foreign language classroom anxiety and enjoyment.
items.authors: Yu X, Zhou Q.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Foreign language classroom anxiety and enjoyment are moderately negatively related, but this relationship has been examined almost entirely at the total score level, and to our knowledge, no published study has asked which specific anxiety experiences are most closely coupled to enjoyment.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Using item-level psychological network analysis and the GGMNIRA simulated node-manipulation framework, we estimated the joint network of eight anxiety items and nine enjoyment items in 3,957 Chinese non-English-major college students and simulated the alleviation of each anxiety node in turn.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Rank-based stability was high (case-dropping correlation stability coefficient ≥ 0.75 for EI, BEI, and the KL rankings). The highest expected influence nodes were shared jokes and topics and teacher support; among anxiety items, panic without preparation speaking ranked highest. The simulations applied two complementary criteria that answer different questions: panic without preparation produced the largest distributional reconfiguration of the enjoyment construct, whereas alleviating nervousness when speaking predicted the largest signed enjoyment gain, the largest model-implied gain among the eight anxiety items. The highest bridge-centrality anxiety node showed negligible simulated effects.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Speaking-related anxiety, particularly the fear of speaking without preparation, is the anxiety experience most closely coupled to enjoyment. Simulated conditioning offers a principled, model-implied complement to centrality when researchers generate hypotheses about which anxiety experiences classroom practice might target first.

items.title: Reality stabilization: a unified framework for psychosis and post-psychotic depression.
items.authors: Panov G, Panova P.

sections.text: Both quantum mechanics and cognitive neuroscience challenge the classical view of a passively perceived reality. Instead, they suggest that reality arises through a process of selection and stabilization from a field of possibilities. This article proposes that this "reality stabilization" framework can unify our understanding of psychosis and post-psychotic depression-two conditions that are currently studied as distinct phenomena, and which existing models of predictive coding, dopaminergic dysregulation, and network neuroscience rarely integrate into a single account. We conceptualize psychosis as a failure of neurocognitive decoherence, in which competing perceptual and interpretative states cannot be reduced to a single, coherent reality. Post-psychotic depression, in contrast, is framed as a compensatory hyperstabilization, in which a rigid, negatively valenced reality is restored, possibly mediated by altered DMN activity. The framework suggests that effective intervention must move beyond dopaminergic blockade to include strategies that promote adaptive network coherence and cognitive integration. The model remains hypothetical, and direct empirical evidence for decoherence-like processes, network changes, and the proposed temporal progression is limited. Future work should focus on empirical testing of stabilization and hyperstabilization mechanisms, longitudinal assessment across illness stages, and their possible therapeutic relevance.

items.title: Associations between latent classes of left-behind experience and non-suicidal self-injury among rural adolescents: the sequential mediating roles of family functioning and shame.
items.authors: Mi W, Tan S, Gao Z, Yang Q, Wang C.

sections.text: This study aimed to identify latent classes of left-behind experience among rural Chinese adolescents and to examine the sequential mediating roles of family functioning and shame in the relationship between left-behind experience and NSSI. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 1,735 rural middle school students with left-behind experience from two schools in Hunan Province, China, in 2024. Latent class analysis (LCA) was performed to identify subgroups of left-behind experience based on four indicators: age at parental separation, parental migration pattern, duration of parental migration, and frequency of communication with migrant parents. Correlation analysis, multiple linear regression, and a bootstrap-based sequential mediation model with 5,000 resamples were used to examine the relationships among latent class membership, family functioning, shame, and NSSI. LCA identified three distinct latent classes of left-behind experience: a low-risk group, a moderate-risk group, and a high-risk group. Correlation analyses showed that latent class membership was significantly associated with family functioning (ρ = -0.149, p < 0.05), shame (ρ = 0.139, p < 0.001), and NSSI (ρ = 0.142, p < 0.05). Family functioning was negatively associated with shame (r = -0.132, p < 0.001) and NSSI (r = -0.235, p < 0.001), whereas shame was positively associated with NSSI (r = 0.256, p < 0.001). Multiple regression analyses indicated that family functioning was negatively associated with shame (β = -0.126, p < 0.001) and NSSI (β = -0.204, p < 0.001), while shame was positively associated with NSSI (β = 0.229, p < 0.001). Sequential mediation analyses further indicated that, compared with the high-risk group, both the low-risk group (B = -0.107, 95% CI: -0.243 to -0.016) and the moderate-risk group (B = -0.143, 95% CI: -0.306 to -0.027) were associated with lower NSSI levels through the sequential pathway involving family functioning and shame. Left-behind experience among rural adolescents is heterogeneous, and different patterns are associated with varying levels of NSSI risk. Significant indirect associations involving family functioning and shame were observed between left-behind experience and NSSI, including a sequential indirect association through family functioning and shame. These findings suggest that family functioning and shame may represent relevant psychosocial factors to consider in future prevention efforts targeting NSSI among high-risk left-behind adolescents.

items.title: The gut-brain axis in Binge Eating Disorder: From microbial dysbiosis to vagal dysfunction and therapeutic intervention.
items.authors: Rossetti C, Aeschlimann L, Praz L, Boutrel B.

sections.text: Binge Eating Disorder (BED), the most prevalent eating disorder worldwide, is characterized by recurrent episodes of uncontrolled food intake accompanied by marked psychological distress in the absence of regular compensatory behaviors. While behavioral and neurobiological frameworks have traditionally dominated research, converging evidence now positions the gut microbiota as a critical mediator of BED pathophysiology through bidirectional microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA) communication. This review synthesizes current knowledge of gut microbial remodeling in BED, elucidating how compositional alterations contribute to pathogenesis through disrupted satiety signaling, altered neurotransmitter metabolism, immune-inflammatory cascades, and vagal dysfunction. Recent evidence highlights BED-specific depletion of fermentative taxa, including Pediococcus, Catenibacterium, and Megasphaera, with depletion of Pediococcus correlated with reduced cardiac vagal tone. The mechanistic landscape encompasses short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-mediated appetite modulation, α -MSH mimicry by bacterial caseinolytic protease B, serotonin and GABA pathways, and immune activation via lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Emerging microbiota-targeted therapeutic strategies, including prebiotics, probiotics, synbiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), are critically evaluated in light of current evidence from BED and related eating disorders. Despite the promising mechanistic rationale, rigorous clinical trials remain scarce. This review highlights several priorities for future research, and the development of precision medicine strategies integrating established therapeutic approaches with emerging microbiota-targeted interventions.

items.title: Longitudinal reference data for the German D-AMI in major depression and healthy controls: implications for future ECT research.
items.authors: Kayser S, Plewnia C, Adan M, Schaaf R, Fallgatter AJ.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is an effective treatment for major depressive disorder (MDD). Retrograde autobiographical memory impairment is considered one of the clinically relevant adverse effects of ECT; however, no validated German instrument is available to assess autobiographical memory. Although longitudinal autobiographical memory data are available from previous studies of patients with depression not receiving ECT, corresponding reference data for the German-language AMI-SF have not been established. This study evaluated the feasibility and interrater reliability of the German Autobiographical Memory Interview-Short Form (D-AMI) and established longitudinal reference data in MDD and healthy controls.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Sixty participants (30 patients with MDD and 30 healthy controls), none of whom received ECT during the observation period, completed the D-AMI at baseline and after a 6-week interval. Feasibility was assessed by completion rates and missing data. Interrater reliability was evaluated in a subset (n = 10) using a two-way random-effects intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Longitudinal performance was quantified using D-AMI score change and its baseline-normalized expression, retrieval consistency. Associations between autobiographical memory measures and depressive symptom severity were explored.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The D-AMI demonstrated a 100% completion rate with no missing data. Interrater reliability was ICC[2,1] = 0.71 (95% CI = 0.17-0.92), indicating considerable uncertainty. The magnitude of longitudinal inconsistency was greater in patients with MDD than in healthy controls, although this between-group difference should be interpreted cautiously because study site and rater were confounded with group.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The D-AMI is a feasible instrument for assessing autobiographical memory in German-speaking populations, while the preliminary interrater reliability estimate requires confirmation in larger samples. The observed magnitude of longitudinal D-AMI inconsistency provides reference information for repeated assessments in the absence of ECT; however, the between-group difference requires cautious interpretation because group, site, and rater effects could not be separated. These findings provide the first longitudinal reference data for the German D-AMI and indicate that changes in autobiographical memory scores should not automatically be interpreted as evidence of ECT-related memory impairment. Rather, such changes should be considered in the context of test-retest variability and retrieval consistency.

items.title: Investigating the Relationship Between Self-Compassion and Marital Satisfaction in Pregnant Women With Depression: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Ashabi B, Haseli A, Rezaeian S, Mahmoodi E, Kamravamanesh M.

sections.text: Antenatal depression is a prevalent mental health concern that can adversely affect marital relationships. Self-compassion has emerged as a potential protective factor in improving psychological health and interpersonal relationships. This cross-sectional study aimed to investigate the relationship between self-compassion and marital satisfaction in pregnant women with depression. In this cross-sectional analytical study, 240 pregnant women with depression were selected through convenience sampling from healthcare centers in Kermanshah, Iran. Depression was assessed using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) with a cutoff score > 12, and all participants met DSM-5 criteria for depressive symptoms. Participants completed the Self-Compassion Scale-Long Form, Hudson's Marital Satisfaction Inventory, and a demographic questionnaire. The cross-sectional design and convenience sampling limit the generalizability of findings. The mean age was 27.68 years (SD = 4.63). Logistic regression revealed that a one-unit increase in total self-compassion score was associated with a 10% increase in the odds of being in the satisfied group (OR = 1.10; 95% CI: 1.07-1.12; p < 0.001). "Common human experience" showed the strongest association (OR = 1.64; 95% CI: 1.43-1.87; p < 0.001). Positive components-self-kindness (r = 0.552), common humanity (r = 0.561), and well-being (r = 0.519)-had significant positive correlations with marital satisfaction, while negative components-self-judgment (r = -0.462), isolation (r = -0.506), and over-identification (r = -0.446)-showed significant negative correlations (all p < 0.001). Self-compassion, particularly its positive components, is significantly associated with higher marital satisfaction in depressed pregnant women. Self-compassion-based interventions may be a promising strategy to improve marital relationship quality and maternal mental health during pregnancy.

items.title: Substance use disorder-associated tricuspid endocarditis: Staged surgery from valvectomy to replacement.
items.authors: Crane JG, Endo T, Trivedi JR, Ganzel BL, Shah S, Pahwa SV, Slaughter MS, Gallo M.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: Optimal surgical treatment of infective tricuspid infective endocarditis (TVIE) is controversial in the setting of active substance use. This study evaluated patients who had endocarditis that was not amenable to tricuspid valve repair. In these patients, a valvectomy was performed to remove the diseased tissue. Patients were then offered a subsequent tricuspid valve replacement after proper follow-up and drug abstinence.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A single-center database was queried (2015-2025) to identify adults who underwent valvectomy for TVIE not amenable to repair after failed medical therapy and persistent positive blood cultures. Patients who underwent valvectomy with documented intravenous drug abstinence for 6 months were considered for staged tricuspid valve replacement (sTVR). Patients with persistent drug use did not receive further surgical treatment. Baseline characteristics, outcomes, and survival were evaluated.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: In total, 153 patients underwent surgical treatment for TVIE. Tricuspid valvectomy was required in 51 patients. Of the patients, 66% were female, with a median age of 30 years. There were 2 operative mortalities (3.9%). The 1-, 5-, and 8-year survival was 91%, 62%, and 51%, respectively; 26 (51%) received an sTVR and 25 (49%) did not receive sTVR (non-sTVR). In those that received an sTVR, there were 0 operative mortalities, median postoperative length of stay was 6 days, and median hours in the intensive care unit was 30. Intravenous drug use relapse after sTVR was present in 57.7% of patients. Survival at 1 and 5 years after the sTVR was 100% and 60%.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Tricuspid valvectomy is an acceptable initial treatment in high-risk patients. Tricuspid valve replacement after completing an abstinence program from intravenous drugs for 6 months has acceptable outcomes in a complex patient population. Further study of long-term outcomes is warranted.

items.title: The Complexity of Deep Acting: A Study of Emotional Labor in Frontline Human Service Work.
items.authors: Singh D, Repchuck R, Monaghan J.

sections.text: This study examines the mental health impacts of emotional labor using an integrated analytical model that considers both job-level emotional labor requirements (negative and positive display rules) and psychological processes of emotion regulation (deep acting and surface acting). Using data from the 2021 Emotions Matter Survey ( n = 854) of mental health and library workers in Ontario, Canada, we explore the conditions under which emotional labor requirements negatively impact mental health. Our findings reveal that negative display rules significantly increase anxiety, and surface acting exacerbates both anxiety and anger. Contrary to expectations, deep acting did not serve as a protective factor for mental health but showed a complex interaction with negative display rules, worsening psychological states under high negative emotional demands. This research underscores the intricate nature of emotional labor's impact on mental health, highlighting the need for context-specific strategies to support frontline workers in emotionally intensive roles.

items.title: Comprehensive artificial intelligence-assisted mental health program for university students in China (CAMPUS): study protocol for a multi-center prospective cohort with planned embedded randomized intervention trials.
items.authors: Yang G, Liu R, Wang C, Zhu R, Qin S, Yan J, Wang Y, Pei H, Liang L, Su Y, Wang S, Wu W, Ji G, Wang F, Wei Y.

sections.text: University students face a rising prevalence of depression, anxiety, insomnia, and suicidal ideation that exceeds the capacity of conventional, resource-constrained campus support services. Although artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted screening tools have emerged, many have evaluated selected modalities or isolated prediction tasks, and their integration with prospectively evaluated intervention pathways remains limited. This protocol describes the Comprehensive Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Mental Health Program for University Students in China (CAMPUS), a multi-center research program comprising a five-year prospective cohort, eight planned embedded randomized controlled trials, and exploratory multimodal AI and multi-omics studies across seven Chinese universities. Longitudinal cohort enrolment commenced at Henan Medical University in September 2025 and is planned to expand across seven participating universities. items.title: Professional future expectations and mental health in university students: a psychosocial and environmental approach.
items.authors: Gaspar T, Cerqueira A, Botelho Guedes F, Aires E, Matias CN, Oliveira C, Rodrigues AT, Jongenelen I.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: University students face heightened risks regarding mental health, with depression, anxiety, and stress being the most prevalent issues. Students' mental health is associated with their academic performance and psychosocial well-being, as well as with their development and future professional trajectories.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This study is part of the Iberian Observatory of Healthy Learning and Youth Participation (OIASP-J) and uses the Healthy Learning Environments Ecosystems instrument. The sample consisted of included 2,315 university students, of whom 65.5% ( n  = 1,516) were female, with a mean age of 22.9 years ( SD  = 5.18).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Older male students who value institutional ethics and values, demonstrate greater academic engagement, report higher levels of well-being, more effective stress management, and greater happiness, exhibit fewer psychosocial risks related to well-being and mental health. Social isolation emerged as a significant factor associated with greater vulnerability in well-being and mental health. Regarding professional future expectation, students with more positive expectations exhibited better individual, psychosocial, and organizational indicators than those with more negative expectations.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: We conclude that the results provide evidence for higher education institutions, health professionals, and policymakers to invest in more skills programs and mental health interventions. These programs may help students thrive academically, maintain good mental health throughout their studies, and successfully complete their training. In turn, this facilitates a smooth transition into professional life and enables students to contribute to society.

items.title: Exploring the Integration of Trauma- and Violence-Informed Research Principles in Longitudinal Youth Mental Health Research: An Arts-Based Protocol.
items.authors: Bernier A, de Snoo Z, Masood N, Bayati JA, Gallagher L, Kimber M.
items.journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Youths' engagement and participation experiences within quantitative, longitudinal mental health studies remain underexplored. Youth with complex mental health needs have unique research participation experiences, underscoring the need for research approaches that strengthen relationality, trust, and engagement. Trauma- and violence-informed research (TVIR) principles offer a promising framework to address these challenges; however, youth-centred perspectives on how TVIR is operationalized within longitudinal mental health research remains limited.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: CALM STORY will explore youths' perspectives and experiences of participating in longitudinal quantitative mental health research that is grounded in TVIR principles, with attention to choice, collaboration, connection, and control.

sections.heading: Design
sections.text: This protocol outlines CALM STORY, a qualitative, arts-based longitudinal evaluation of youth participation in the Cohort Network of AdoLescents and youth with Multiple mental health conditions (CALM) Master Observational Trial (MOT). CALM STORY is theoretically organised around both TVIR principles as well as the Lundy Model of Participation.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We are purposefully sampling 30 youth aged 11-19 years enroled in the CALM MOT. Youth are completing two semi-structured qualitative interviews and a PhotoVoice workshop series. With consent, we will extract key socio-demographic data from the CALM MOT to contextualise TVIR strategies. Data will be managed using NVivo software and thematically analysed using a framework-based analytic approach guided by TVIR principles and the Lundy Model of participation.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: CALM STORY will generate youth-centred insights into TVIR engagement and participation in longitudinal quantitative mental health research. Findings will inform key deliverables, including the development and scaling TVIR training for research teams, as well as a research policy brief to be disseminated to the CALM MOT network, research ethics boards, and research funders.

sections.heading: Patient or public contribution
sections.text: A Youth Advisory Group (YAG) comprised of youth with lived experience of multiple mental health conditions was established to consult on the CALM MOT's design, data collection, knowledge mobilisation, and sub-studies. The YAG informed CALM STORY's study design, including the interview and PhotoVoice guides and will continued to be consulted throughout the study and its dissemination activities.

items.title: Barriers to survivorship care for adolescent and young adult cancer survivors: perspectives of survivors and cancer specialists.
items.authors: Kojima Y, Ando Y, Nogami Y, Iwata S, Suzuki T, Satomi E.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Adolescent and young adult (AYA) cancer survivors have complex long-term survivorship needs beyond cancer recurrence surveillance. Although survivor concerns and healthcare provider perspectives have been reported separately, few studies have evaluated both within the same healthcare setting. We conducted complementary surveys of AYA cancer survivors and physicians to characterize survivorship concerns, barriers to long-term follow-up (LTFU), and telemedicine preferences.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This single-center, cross-sectional study included questionnaire surveys of 98 AYA cancer survivors receiving outpatient follow-up after cancer treatment and 45 physicians involved in AYA survivorship care at the National Cancer Center Hospital, Japan. Survivors were surveyed regarding LTFU, survivorship concerns, and telemedicine preferences, and physicians regarding LTFU practices, referral barriers, and AYA-specific challenges. Associations between survivor characteristics and telemedicine preference were explored using univariable analyses.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among survivors, 84 of 98 (85.7%) considered LTFU necessary, and 51 (52.0%) reported difficulty attending follow-up because of school or work commitments. Of 91 survivors evaluable for telemedicine preference, 69 (75.8%) were likely or somewhat likely to use at least one telemedicine service. Among all 98 survivors, frequently selected telemedicine topics included disease information (45.9%), daily activities (31.6%), anxiety and worry (30.6% each), financial issues (29.6%), and work- or school-related concerns (27.6%). No demographic, clinical, treatment-related or healthcare utilization factors were significantly associated with telemedicine preference. Among physicians, 13 of 44 (29.5%) reported an established departmental LTFU policy. Follow-up at the treating cancer center was supported by 76.2% for survivors at high risk of recurrence but by only 21.4% for all AYA survivors. Major barriers to coordinated care included difficulty identifying hospitals providing cancer-specific LTFU (73.8%) or multidisciplinary care (71.4%). Physicians identified reproductive medicine and life events as major AYA-specific challenges and mental health, endocrine disorders, and sexual and reproductive health as areas requiring additional support.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: AYA cancer survivors reported substantial survivorship concerns, whereas physicians identified barriers to coordinated multidisciplinary care. Telemedicine was of interest to many survivors and warrants prospective evaluation as a potential component of multidisciplinary survivorship care.

items.title: Monitoring patient progress and changes in patient and clinician reported symptoms with measurement informed care in a pediatric primary care mental health integration program.
items.authors: Adams DP, Schweitzer J, Holt JR, Bird AF, Carr-Lee N, Hollenbach KA.

sections.text: Measurement informed care (MIC) utilizes validated instruments to screen and monitor patient symptoms and has been shown to improve patient outcomes and streamline diagnostic processes. Our primary care mental health integration (PCMHI) program embedded mental health clinicians in the pediatric primary care setting to increase access to mental healthcare and provide care for adolescents. The purpose of this study was to identify changes in patients' self-reported symptom severity and determine whether provider assessments of patient progress were associated with patients' completed screening scores between the initial and final visits of short-term treatment within a PCMHI program. Patients were retrospective from a multisite pediatric PCMHI program. The program's standardized measures included the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) for patients older than 12 years and the Pediatric Symptom Checklist-17 (PSC-17) for patients younger than 12 years. Before each PCMHI session, patients completed self-reported assessments, and after the session, clinicians provided a score reflecting overall patient progress. Data from treated patients were extracted from electronic medical records, and changes in patient scores were calculated and analyzed using Stata 16.1 (College Station, TX). A total of 2,702 patients were eligible for analysis. Significant reductions (95% CIs) in the proportion of patients scoring above clinically relevant cutoffs were observed for the PHQ-9 (28.8%; 26.1-31.5%), GAD-7 (25.8%; 23.4-28.4%), PSC-17 attention subscale (16.5%; 14.6-18.6%), and PSC-17 internalizing subscale (17.3%; 15.3-19.4%) (all p < 0.001). No significant change was identified for the PSC-17 externalizing subscale (11.0%; 9.4-12.8%; p = 0.19). Effect sizes for score change among patients above the clinical cutoff were large (r = 0.68-0.80 across the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 severity scores), and the odds of moving below the cutoff exceeded the odds of moving above it for every measure except the externalizing subscale. CGI improvement scores were significantly correlated with the PHQ-9, GAD-7, and each of the PSC-17 subscales (all p < 0.001). Validated mental health assessments, completed by patients before their appointments, documented reductions in symptom severity over brief, short-term treatment and changes in patient- and clinician-completed assessments were significantly correlated. These results demonstrate the feasibility of using patient-provided self-assessments to monitor patient progress.

items.title: Physical exercise and mobile phone addiction in college students: negative emotions and coping styles as chain mediators.
items.authors: Guo S, Tong W, Zhou X, Wang S, Shen P, Meng S.

sections.text: Considering the significant risks that widespread mobile phone addiction poses to the holistic health of college students, further research is essential. This article systematically explores correlational mechanisms linking physical exercise engagement to mobile phone addiction. Furthermore, it evaluates how Negative Emotions and Coping Styles function as mediators in this relationship. A convenience sampling approach was employed to recruit 3,283 undergraduates across the first 3 years of college. Data collection took place between April and May 2025, during which participants self-reported their engagement in physical exercise, problematic mobile phone use patterns, psychological distress (manifested as depression, anxiety, and stress symptoms), as well as their preferred coping styles. All responses were gathered through the Wenjuanxing online survey platform. For the statistical analysis, SPSS 29.0 was utilized to compute descriptive statistics and bivariate correlations. Furthermore, to evaluate the sequential mediation effect, we adopted Hayes' PROCESS macro (version 4.1, Model 6), implementing a bootstrapping approach with 5,000 iterations to generate bias-corrected confidence intervals for the indirect pathways. Students showed low physical exercise (M = 18.49 ± 14.90) and variable mobile phone addiction (M = 35.40 ± 14.78). Physical exercise negatively correlated with addiction (r = -0.83), negative emotions (r = -0.39), and negative coping styles (r = -0.39), but positively with positive coping (r = 0.31). Negative emotions positively predicted addiction (r = 0.618). Mediation analysis showed physical exercise exhibited a correlational link with lower addiction levels (direct effect = 21.54%) through three distinct indirect correlational pathways. The path through negative emotions was dominant (72.45%), while coping-related paths accounted for 1.41%-4.6%. The independent mediating contribution of positive coping styles was slightly larger than that of negative coping styles; the dominant explanatory power across both models stemmed from the pathway of negative emotions. Correlational results preliminarily suggest that physical exercise may be negatively associated with college students' mobile phone addiction through correlational pathways including sequential serial paths involving negative emotions and two types of coping styles. The present correlational data could provide empirical reference for developing sports-based mental health interventions.

items.title: Exploring stigma of physical health conditions across low and lower-middle income countries: a secondary analysis of a global systematic review.
items.authors: Ram B, Elagandula V, Counts L, Zabotka L, Williams A, Wynja K, Malone S, Graetz DE.

sections.text: Stigma undermines health equity by impeding engagement in care and worsening outcomes. Systematic reviews of stigma are primarily from high-income countries, focus on specific conditions, especially mental illness, and employ heterogeneous stigma measures. Despite bearing a disproportionate burden of disease, low-income (LIC) and lower-middle-income (LMIC) countries remain underrepresented in existing reviews. This study characterizes stigma definitions, measures, impacts, and interventions in physical health conditions across LICs and LMICs. This secondary analysis included 137 publications, previously identified through a global systematic review, reporting on patient or caregiver stigma of physical health conditions among LIC/LMIC populations. Data on definitions, measurements, and interventions were utilized from a primary review. Two reviewers extracted supplemental data regarding the study's conceptualization and outcomes and conducted a quality appraisal. Among the 137 studies (32 LIC, 105 LMIC), 75.2% used cross-sectional designs, 67.2% focused on adults, and 75.9% included populations with communicable diseases, including HIV, TB, and leprosy. Stigma definitions and measures varied widely, with uneven coverage of stigma dimensions. Negative mental health outcomes were commonly associated with stigma related to physical conditions (57.7%). Only 13.1% of studies evaluated stigma interventions, primarily including social support or health education, with heterogenous intervention designs, outcome definitions, and follow-up periods. Our quality appraisal demonstrated limited use of population-validated and culturally adapted stigma tools. Stigma research in LIC/LMICs has primarily been conducted in middle-income countries and focused on adults with communicable diseases, leaving gaps for stigma research in non-communicable diseases and pediatric populations. Future work should prioritize development of culturally adapted stigma frameworks and measures to improve patient outcomes in LIC/LMICs. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42023433176.

items.title: Recentring young people in AI for mental health support: breaking the evidence-design feedback loop.
items.authors: Sangha JK, Partridge SR, Raeside R.

sections.text: Young people are largely underrepresented in research underpinning AI-based mental health tools. AI systems are shaped by evidence bases that do not always fully incorporate young people's opinions and perspectives. We propose a conceptual model, an evidence-design feedback loop in which exclusion from research may risk producing interventions that are less likely to be adopted by young people or meet their needs. These risks are amplified for young people from marginalised and underrepresented cultural contexts who face compounded exclusion, as the evidence base and design processes often lack cultural diversity. The relationships in this model are hypothesised from existing literature. This article argues that structural change is required across both research and industry to incorporate co-design with young people. AI developers should demonstrate meaningful involvement of young people from the earliest stages of development, and regulators should enforce higher regulatory standards in this respect. Researchers and AI developers should embed meaningful co-design with young people into the development of AI-based mental health tools which may help these technologies to be more relevant, safe and responsive to young people's lived experiences.

The relationships in this model are hypothesised from existing literature. This article argues that structural change is required across both research and industry to incorporate co-design with young people. AI developers should demonstrate meaningful involvement of young people from the earliest stages of development, and regulators should enforce higher regulatory standards in this respect. Researchers and AI developers should embed meaningful co-design with young people into the development of AI-based mental health tools which may help these technologies to be more relevant, safe and responsive to young people's lived experiences.

items.title: Hepatitis C Micro-Elimination Through Patient Navigation of Individuals Experiencing Elevated Risk in a Mid-Atlantic Regional Healthcare System in 2022 and 2023: A Cohort Study.
items.authors: Visconti A, Garner D, Gabra J, Fernandez S.

sections.heading: Background and aims
sections.text: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) disproportionately impacts persons with substance use and mental health disorders. Micro-elimination projects selectively foster diagnosis, treatment and reinfection of high priority demographic groups. A small-scale, peer navigation focused micro-elimination project was launched at a regional multidisciplinary and multispecialty health system in the Mid-Atlantic to facilitate treatment engagement for high-risk individuals.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The program used electronic medical record (EMR) periodic surveillance and navigation of individuals diagnosed with HCV and either not engaged, or not completed, treatment, as well as those needing additional testing (for either sustained virologic response or high-risk re-testing). Specialist appointments and referrals for associated behavioral health interventions were provided. Historical propensity score matched controls were utilized to provide a comparator population.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Between April 2022 and July 2023, 115 persons were navigated, including 78 persons without a prior specialist appointment (New Patients), 15 persons previously engaged with a specialist but not completing treatment, and 22 patients needing additional testing. Among New Patients, 52.6% of patients attended treatment appointments, 28.2% started treatment, and 14.1% had a confirmed undetectable HCV test. Compared to historical matched controls, persons navigated were almost twice as likely to attend an appointment (HR: 1.96 [1.18-3.23], p  = 0.008), and nearly three times more likely to start treatment (HR: 2.86 [1.41-5.79], p  = 0.003). The median time from navigation to an appointment for New Patients was 71 days, and 143 days until starting treatment.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: A small-scale, peer-navigation focused micro-navigation program successfully engaged patients but had mixed success in successfully navigating the care cascade. Despite navigation and consistent engagement, nearly half of patients dropped off at each step of the care cascade. Compared to historical controls, patients were more likely to make appointments and initiate treatment. Future efforts should be targeted at reducing times for specialist appointments and expanding treatment at diagnosis location.

items.title: Mental health literacy among Arab-Palestinians in Israel and its association with socioeconomic characteristics and healthcare utilization.
items.authors: Abo-Ras N, Youngmann R, Neter E.
items.journal: Israel journal of health policy research

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Research on Mental Health Literacy (MHL) has expanded across cultural minority groups, yet little is known about the relationships between socioeconomic status (SES), MHL, and mental health (MH) service utilization. This study investigates the relationship between MHL, SES, and MH service utilization among Palestinian citizens of Israel (PCIs).

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional survey (n = 372, M_age 36.88 ± 13.52 years, 68% female), based on the Australian National Survey of Mental Health Literacy and Stigma, examined associations between SES indicators (education and income), MHL components, and MH service utilization. Compared to the PCI population, the sample included more women, older people, and more people with higher education.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Higher SES, as assessed by both indicators, was significantly associated with greater mental health literacy (MHL) at the bivariate level, particularly in terms of accurate disorder identification, knowledge of appropriate interventions, and lower levels of stigma. Hierarchical logistic regression revealed that education and income were significantly associated with MH service use (OR = 3.62, 95% CI: 1.38-9.45; OR = 0.36, 95% CI: 0.13-0.99, respectively), and first-aid MHL knowledge also contributed to explaining variance (OR = 0.86, 95% CI: 0.75-0.99). Other MHL indices, such as stigma and knowledge of potential helpers, were not significantly associated with service utilization.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The findings underscore the interplay between structural inequalities and cultural beliefs in shaping MH knowledge and behavior, and highlight the need for culturally sensitive, socioeconomically accessible interventions to improve MH outcomes in minority populations. The authors advocate for integrating MHL education into secondary educational settings and implementing policy reforms that address both material disparities and cultural barriers to care. These insights contribute to the global discourse on MH disparities in indigenous and marginalized communities.

items.title: Promoting Positive Adolescent Mental Health (PPAMH!) for School Climate: protocol for a feasibility randomised control trial in secondary schools.
items.authors: Wadman R, Taylor O, Hudson K, Lewer D, Hewitt C, Pickavance J, Pryce J, Wright J, Gilbody S.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: We describe a feasibility randomised controlled trial to determine if it is possible to implement a full cluster-randomised trial of a multi-component whole-school intervention aiming to improve the school climate. The Promoting Positive Adolescent Mental Health (PPAMH!) intervention will be adapted from an intervention previously trialled in India and Australia that reduced bullying, depression and risk behaviours among students.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We will randomise six secondary schools in Bradford in a feasibility trial. Three schools will receive the intervention and three will act as the 'usual care' control condition. We will collect quantitative and qualitative data on the implementation through activity logs and interviews with staff and well-being mentors. We will determine the feasibility of accessing and using routine education data and self-report mental health data as outcomes in the full trial.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: This study will provide information about the acceptability and feasibility of delivering and evaluating the school climate intervention in secondary schools.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This is the first study to deliver a promising whole school climate intervention in the UK. The results of this feasibility trial will inform the decision to embark on a full trial and further intervention adaptations as needed. Trial registration ISRCTN registry reference ISRCTN14856201.

items.title: Acute exercise for emotional pattern separation in youth with psychiatric symptoms and childhood adversity: a randomized controlled trial.
items.authors: Mazereel V, Jennen L, Vancampfort D, Qiao Z, Vansteelandt K, Dupont P, Lecei A, van Winkel R.

sections.text: Adolescence and young adulthood are critical periods for the emergence of transdiagnostic psychiatric symptoms. Pattern separation (PS) is the ability to discriminate between similar stimuli. Its behavioral proxy is mnemonic discrimination. PS is an important hippocampal function impaired in several mental disorders. Previous research demonstrated that while childhood adversity might lead to impaired PS, acute exercise could enhance it. Using a randomized controlled design, we examined the effect of acute moderate-intensity exercise on PS versus a rest condition in a group of young people. Building on our prior report in a healthy youth sample (Jennen et al., 2025), the present study examines adolescents and young adults with transdiagnostic psychiatric symptoms and childhood adversity, compared to healthy controls. We integrated behavioral and neural PS with an emotional mnemonic discrimination task and functional magnetic resonance imaging. Our analyses did not reveal significant effects of exercise or psychiatric symptoms on mnemonic discrimination and PS. Additionally, PS was not associated with symptom dimensions or childhood adversity. Across groups, we observed decreased discrimination for positive images and increased neural activation in the left centromedial amygdala for emotional images. No correlation between neural activity and mnemonic discrimination could be observed and exploratory analyses revealed no neural activity consistent with PS. We conclude that in our study neither mnemonic discrimination nor PS was associated with psychiatric symptoms or childhood adversity in adolescents and young adults with transdiagnostic psychiatric symptoms. In addition, acute exercise had no effect. Future research should prioritize establishing robust and reliable associations of both acute exercise and psychiatric symptoms with mnemonic discrimination and neural PS.

items.title: Impact of Medical-Educational Collaboration on School-Based Mental Health Support in Japan.
items.authors: Ohashi K, Mitani M, Kurumai M, Yamada R, Tsujino R, Takano T, Sakata M, Nagai Y, Yamada A.
items.journal: Pediatrics international : official journal of the Japan Pediatric Society

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: In Japan, school-based mental health support is becoming increasingly critical, owing to rising rates of school non-attendance and suicide among students. However, barriers in accessing medical facilities remain high. In Nagoya, the "Children's Advocacy Committee" has implemented a medical-educational collaboration model. This study evaluated the impact of physician participation in school case review meetings and observation of outpatient consultations on the support skills of school-based professionals.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: An anonymous self-administered questionnaire was distributed to 178 members of the Children's Advocacy Committee who participated in the collaboration program in fiscal year 2025. The participants rated the degree of change in their interactions with students, parents, and school and medical staff using a 5-point Likert scale.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A high percentage of the 155 respondents reported positive changes across all categories. In the case review meetings, 68% perceived positive changes in support approaches toward students. In outpatient observations, 72% perceived positive changes in support approaches toward parents. Spearman's rank correlation analysis revealed significant negative correlations between years of professional experience and the degree of perceived change, particularly for outpatient observations (e.g., students: ρ = -0.395, p < 0.01). This indicates that staff members with fewer years of experience perceived greater benefits from the program.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Both collaborative activities were associated with perceived positive changes in support approaches among school-based professionals. The clinical exposure provided by outpatient observations was particularly impactful for early-career staff. Establishing a tiered collaborative system tailored to professional experience can further strengthen school-based mental health support.

items.title: Effects of Psychotherapy on Quality of Life among Patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis.
items.authors: Subramaniam Y, Ooi PB, Hoo MX, Wong YY, Phang K, Ali RAR, Pickup R.
items.journal: The Malaysian journal of medical sciences : MJMS

sections.text: Individuals diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) have been known to have diminished quality of life (QoL). This present study aimed to examine the impact of psychotherapy on the QoL of patients with IBD. A systematic search for studies was conducted through a total of six databases, namely, MEDLINE, PubMed, Scopus, SAGE, ProQuest (psychology database), and ProQuest (public health database) from their date of inception up to 20 March 2024. The inclusion criteria were studies on patients with IBD, carried out through a randomised controlled trial design, published in the English language, and with full-text content available online. Two researchers independently extracted articles that met the selection criteria and evaluated the quality of each study. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted, and data were presented in weighted mean difference (WMD) with a 95% CI. Fourteen studies were included in the systematic review, of which three were included in the meta-analysis. Overall, while psychotherapy showed no significant improvements in some QoL domains such as clinical bowel condition and systemic symptoms, notable enhancements were observed in social functioning and overall QoL. The findings underscore the importance of integrating psychotherapeutic approaches into IBD management to address psychological and social challenges, thereby enhancing overall patient well-being. These results have significant implications for clinical mental health counsellors and future research in IBD care.

items.title: The 2026 Oceania Report of the MJA-Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change: Children Already Impacted, With a Lifetime of Exposure to Come.
items.authors: Beggs PJ, Singh T, Bambrick H, Borchers Arriagada N, Bowen K, Capon AG, Colagiuri P, Crandon T, Cross TJ, Dimer L, Green D, Hanigan IC, Heenan M, Ho T, Jay O, Kennard HR, Langridge F, Linnenluecke MK, Lokmic-Tomkins Z, Lovett R, MacGregor C, Malik A, Markey-Towler R, Matthews V, McKay CD, McMichael C, Nice K, Peel J, Seneviratne S, Sievert K, Smallcombe J, Stevenson M, Trueck S, Vardoulakis S, Vyas A, Wilkes B, Williams JTW, Woodward AJ, Zhang Y, Hasan MM, Romanello MB.

sections.text: The Medical Journal of Australia (MJA)-Lancet Countdown on health and climate change in Oceania was established in 2017 and produced its first regional assessment in 2018 and annual updates from 2019 to 2025. It examines five broad domains: (1) health hazards, exposures and impacts; (2) adaptation, planning and resilience for health; (3) mitigation actions and health co-benefits; (4) economics and finance; and (5) public and political engagement. In this, the eighth report of the MJA-Lancet Countdown, we track an extensive suite of indicators across these five domains, accessing and presenting the latest data and further refining and developing our analyses. Our analyses show that exposure of infants and older adults to heatwaves in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand has increased substantially over the past decade due to climate change, and half of the 16,230 young Australians aged 14-19 years surveyed reported that they are worried or sad about the impacts of climate change, including its threat to people, and about 1 in 7 reported that such feelings are negatively affecting their daily life. Increasing heat-related mortality alone is placing a large economic burden on Australians, with associated inflation-adjusted costs over the period 2021-2025 being more than double what they were at the start of the century, now averaging an estimated US$1.49 billion per year nationally. In other areas, some progress is being made. New Zealand's Health National Adaptation Plan 2024-2027, published in October 2024, lays the foundation for building climate resilience within its health system, while acknowledging the environmental and social determinants of health that apply more broadly. The provision of climate services to the health sector in both Australia and New Zealand is categorised as advanced. In Australia, healthcare-related greenhouse gas emissions generally declined from 2016 to 2023. In conclusion, the threat to physical and mental health from climate change continues to grow. Despite pockets of progress, Australia and New Zealand have a long way to go to adequately mitigate and adapt to climate change, and in so doing not only avoid health impacts but seize the opportunity for generational health gains. Important opportunities have been lost, such as the failed attempts to amend Australia's Climate Change Act 2022 to 'require decision-makers to consider the health and well-being of children in Australia when making significant decisions'. In 2026, Australia is in the spotlight as President of Negotiations for the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31)-an unprecedented opportunity for the Australian Government to push through the sizable step change in global climate action that is now critically required.
