items.title: Pneumocystis jirovecii Pneumonia in an Adolescent With Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Due to Non-adherence to Prophylaxis: A Case Report.
items.authors: Pelcic P, Ruzman L.

sections.text: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP) is a severe and potentially life-threatening opportunistic infection in immunocompromised patients, especially those with hematologic malignancies. Although routine prophylaxis with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) has significantly reduced its incidence, breakthrough infections still occur, most commonly due to poor adherence to prophylactic therapy. This case report highlights the risks of non-adherence to PJP prophylaxis in adolescents and underscores the importance of early diagnostic suspicion and multidisciplinary management. A 15-year-old female patient with acute lymphoblastic leukemia presented during her seventh month of maintenance therapy (methotrexate and 6-mercaptopurine) in a compromised general condition with tachycardia, tachypnea, and hypoxemia, following a 24-hour history of fever and dry cough. Heteroanamnestic data revealed prolonged non-adherence to TMP-SMX prophylaxis. Imaging showed diffuse bilateral interstitial infiltrates on chest radiography and ground-glass opacities on high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT). PJP was confirmed via polymerase chain reaction (PCR) from bronchoalveolar lavage and a positive serum 1,3-β-D-glucan test. Treatment included intravenous TMP-SMX, corticosteroids, and high-flow nasal cannula oxygen therapy. The course was complicated by pancytopenia, likely secondary to TMP-SMX, and febrile neutropenia. A multidisciplinary approach, including social and psychiatric support, addressed non-adherence. The patient was discharged in good condition; maintenance therapy was continued, and prophylaxis was switched to monthly aerosolized pentamidine administered in the hospital setting. PJP prevention in pediatric oncology remains a significant challenge, as inconsistent adherence can rapidly lead to severe clinical deterioration. Our experience suggests that successful outcomes depend on addressing psychosocial barriers early. Transitioning to supervised, hospital-administered alternatives, such as aerosolized pentamidine, alongside multidisciplinary support, may help ensure adherence to prophylaxis in vulnerable oncology patients.

items.title: Psoriatic Arthritis Without Cutaneous Manifestations: A Case of Diagnostic Delay, Pathologic Progression, and Psychological Burden.
items.authors: Tomlinson P, Sauers KN, Nosal E, Davies B, McGarvey CE, Stackhouse J.

sections.text: Psoriatic arthritis (PsA) is a chronic inflammatory musculoskeletal disease. Presentations can vary, but common manifestations include peripheral arthritis, dactylitis, enthesitis, nail changes, and skin changes, including psoriasis. Diagnosis is often challenging due to the absence of specific biomarkers, variable clinical presentation, and overlap with conditions such as osteoarthritis and fibromyalgia. These diagnostic obstacles contribute to frequent misdiagnosis and delay in treatment, which, over time, leads to irreversible joint damage, functional impairment, and increased comorbidities. A 62-year-old woman with a 15-year history of chronic pain attributed to fibromyalgia and osteoarthritis presented to primary care with persistent hand and foot pain and worsening depressive symptoms. Prior treatments failed to provide relief. Imaging and laboratory evaluation were not consistent with her previous diagnoses of fibromyalgia and osteoarthritis. Although she lacked characteristic psoriatic skin lesions, further history revealed a family history of psoriasis in her daughter and grandson. This finding prompted consideration of PsA, and the diagnosis was made based on clinical presentation and history. The patient was started on disease-modifying antirheumatic drug therapy and escitalopram, with significant improvement in both pain and mood within one month. This case exemplifies the impacts of delayed diagnosis in a patient with PsA without cutaneous manifestations. Common misdiagnoses of PsA can include fibromyalgia, osteoarthritis, and rheumatoid arthritis due to overlapping subjective and objective findings, making diagnosis difficult. This delay leads to prolonged initiation of treatment and thus results in further joint damage, functional decline, and mental health impacts. Quicker suspicion and thorough history taking in patients with chronic musculoskeletal pain unresponsive to treatment could potentially improve diagnostic delay trends of PsA, even in the absence of cutaneous findings.

items.title: Understanding the Effects of Drishti Bheda, the Eye Movements in Indian Classical Dance, on Vision, Audition, and Cognition: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Sundarrajan R, M RM, S A, P R, M R.

sections.text: Bharatanatyam is one of India's oldest classical Indian art forms, which integrates the practice of Drishti Bheda, i.e., synchronized controlled scanning eye movements with head, neck, and body movements used to amplify visual articulation and communication. These ocular workouts repeated over time suggest that eye training might boost up information from sight and hearing to cognitive capacities, as well as control and ability to regulate motor imagery, which relates to one's ability to see/feel movement without physical acting, to stimulate mental clarity, mindfulness, and boost emotions via plasticity of neural networks. Although Drishti Beda is artistically relevant to culture and the world of art, it lacks sufficient research to determine the impact on sensorial and cognitive skills. Knowledge of these effects can provide the scientific rationale to include traditional eye movement meditation exercises in preventive healthcare protocols for the brain and the senses and cognitive rehabilitation. This research assessed long-term Bharatanatyam training with Drishti Bheda on visual, auditory, and cognitive performance in healthy young individuals to understand if longer participation in the demanding nature of Bharatanatyam translates into improved sensory processing and overall cognition.  A cross-sectional comparative study was conducted in 60 healthy young females aged 18-22 years after obtaining Institutional Ethics Committee (IEC) clearance. Of the two groups involved, the 30 Bharatanatyam dancers had a formal training period of more than 10 years in dance, whereas their age-matched non-dancing counterparts formed the control group. Demographic and anthropometric assessments were performed on all subjects; the visual aspect of health was studied using critical flicker fusion frequency (CFFF-Maven Labs Pvt. Ltd., Bangalore, India), while the auditory aspect of health was determined using pure tone audiometry (PTA) (RS I digital portable diagnostic audiometer, Sounds Good Hearing Care Scientific Company, Madurai, India); the mental health aspects of health were assessed using the Mindful Attention Awareness Scale (MAAS), Movement Imagery Questionnaire-3 (MIQ-3), the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (ERQ), and the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10). The groups were analyzed using independent-samples t tests. This study found that Bharatanatyam performers exhibited significantly higher CFFF values (visual temporal resolution; p < 0.0001) and PTA thresholds (auditory sensitivity) in the right ear (p = 0.0053) and left ear (p = 0.0006) compared with the control group. Similarly, statistically significant improvements in cognitive measures were observed in dancers in mindfulness (p≈0.0004), perceived stress (p < 0.0001), emotion regulation (p = 0.0013), and movement imagery (p < 0.0001). Long-term Bharatanatyam training, along with Drishti Bheda, was associated with improved visual, auditory, and cognitive abilities in young adult brains. It is likely that the multisensory-training aspect of the performance might involve a variety of neural modifications or plasticity across and within different sensory modalities, and different functional brain areas or systems, involved with attentional control, motor imagination, and emotion-processing abilities.

items.title: Obesity and Poverty in Delaware: The Need for Community Level Interventions.
items.authors: Dillard D, Angalet GB.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: The study aimed to examine the community characteristics of vulnerable communities where obesity is one of the top three chronic conditions with the greatest disparity compared to the Delaware statewide obesity rate to demonstrate the need for community specific education and interventions.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The study is a secondary analysis using a subset of the CHAMG research project dataset and includes 47 vulnerable communities. The dataset included official data reported between 2019 and 2022 and abstracted from My Healthy Communities Delaware data portal and the IP3 data portal.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The study communities differed notably from Delaware's general population and from each other. The average poverty rate was greater (21% compared 11%) and the average obesity rate was greater (41% compared to 34%). The minority population in the study communities ranged from 6% to 93% Black and from 2% to 70% Hispanic. The average age ranged from 27 years old to 54 years old. The poverty rate ranged from 4% to 50%. Eleven (23%) of the vulnerable communities with obesity disparity were rural. Depression and heart disease ranked in the top three most disparate chronic conditions in at least half of the study communities and HPB in 36% of the study communities. Fewer community assets were identified in the study communities, including fewer medical professionals, lower rates of HBP management, and lower English proficiency.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Vulnerable communities with high rates of obesity differ from Delaware's general population. They have fewer community assets and greater prevalence of obesity-related chronic conditions. There is notable variation across the study communities, underscoring the need for community specific education and interventions.

sections.heading: Public health implications
sections.text: Obesity is a key multi-solver health condition. Because obesity is correlated with other chronic conditions, mental health diagnoses, and well-being indicators, community specific obesity education and interventions will likely decrease obesity rates and improve other health and well-being conditions.

items.title: Long-term quality of life, rehospitalization risks, and economic viability of remote cardiac rehabilitation: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.authors: Pei H, Li H, Hu M, Liu B, Hu D, Li Y, Xiao Q.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Although remote cardiac rehabilitation (RCR) is a promising alternative to traditional center-based care, evidence regarding its exact impact on health-related quality of life (HRQoL), cardiovascular safety, and economic viability remains fragmented, necessitating a comprehensive synthesis to guide clinical implementation.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: This systematic review and meta-analysis aim to evaluate the HRQoL, cardiovascular safety, and economic viability of RCR versus standard center-based care in cardiovascular disease, with subgroup analyses based on follow-up duration and high-risk patient cohorts.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Literature searches were conducted across multiple databases, including PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, supplemented by manual screening of relevant references to identify clinical studies on RCR up to July 2026. Two independent review teams performed data extraction and risk of bias assessment using the RevMan software. Meta-analyses were conducted employing random-effects models to calculate pooled effect sizes with corresponding 95% confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was assessed using the Cochrane Q test and I ^2 statistic, and potential publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots and Egger's test. To evaluate the robustness of the pooled results and explore potential heterogeneity, subgroup and fixed-effects sensitivity analyses were conducted, supplemented by trial sequential analysis (TSA).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A total of 45 randomized controlled trials were included in this meta-analysis. RCR significantly improved HRQoL across multiple scales (MacNew: MD = 0.17; MLHFQ: MD = -5.38; P  < 0.05), while maintaining SF-36 and HADS outcomes comparable to standard care. Exploratory analyses indicated statistically significant improvements in mental health at 6 months (MD = 1.73, P  = 0.03) and physical functioning at 12 months (MD = 1.48, P  = 0.0002). Regarding cardiovascular safety, RCR was not associated with a statistically significant increase in the risk of MACEs, all-cause mortality, or adverse events ( P  > 0.05) compared to conventional care. RCR significantly reduced the risk of cardiac rehospitalization (RR = 0.70, P  = 0.01), with exploratory stratified analyses indicating that this favorable association was evident in the hardware-integrated interventions subgroup (RR = 0.59, P  = 0.02) and 6-month observation subgroup (RR = 0.38, P  < 0.00001), alongside a non-significant numerical protective trend among high-risk patients (RR: 0.59 vs. 0.74, P  = 0.15). The economic viability of RCR remains uncertain, critically depending on initial setup outlays, patient scaling, and subsequent healthcare utilization.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: RCR may serve as an effective and safe alternative to conventional care that improves physical and psychological well-being, was associated with a lower risk of cardiac rehospitalization, and may provide economic value in certain healthcare systems.

items.title: Invisible burdens: reframing maternal mental health as a core priority in conflict-affected and low-resource settings.
items.authors: Abdullahi Khalif I, Abdullahi Hubow Y, Omar AM, Dahir NA, Abdi AM.

sections.text: Maternal mental health remains an overlooked dimension of global women's health, particularly in conflict-affected and low-resource settings where psychological distress is intensified by poverty, displacement, violence, gender inequality, and fragile health systems. Although maternal health agendas have achieved progress in reducing mortality, survival-focused approaches often fail to capture the psychological burdens that shape women's well-being, caregiving capacity, and intergenerational outcomes. This Perspective argues that maternal mental health should be reframed as a core component of maternal health rather than a secondary concern. Drawing on a life-course and gender-responsive perspective, we propose a conceptual framework linking conflict and structural inequality with social determinants, maternal psychological outcomes, and consequences for mothers and children. We highlight the need for integrated health-system responses that combine mental health screening, psychosocial support, community-based care, and gender-responsive policies to achieve equitable and sustainable improvements in women's health.

items.title: Beyond seizures: the hidden burden of developmental epileptic encephalopathies.
items.authors: Dell'Isola GB, Sorrentino M, Massara S, Dini G, Salpietro V, Ferrara P, Striano P, Vigevano F, Verrotti A.

sections.text: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) are a group of severe childhood-onset disorders characterized by drug-resistant epilepsy and a broad spectrum of neurodevelopmental, behavioral, psychiatric, and systemic manifestations. Although seizure control has traditionally been the primary therapeutic goal, growing evidence indicates that non-seizure manifestations often represent the main determinants of long-term disability, quality of life, and caregiver burden. This review highlights the hidden burden of DEEs by focusing on three paradigmatic syndromes: Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (LGS), Dravet syndrome (DS), and tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC). DS and LGS represent prototypical DEEs, whereas TSC is a multisystem genetic disorder that is frequently, although not invariably, associated with early-onset drug-resistant epilepsy and DEE-like neurodevelopmental trajectories. Across these conditions, the severity and progression of clinical manifestations are influenced by complex interactions between genetic, structural, developmental, and epileptic mechanisms, supporting the concept that epilepsy and associated manifestations represent interconnected features of a broader neurodevelopmental disorder. The review also emphasizes the substantial psychosocial, physical, and economic burden experienced by families and caregivers, which often exceeds the impact of seizures alone. Current management strategies should therefore extend beyond seizure reduction and adopt a multidisciplinary, life-course approach integrating early genetic diagnosis, syndrome-specific surveillance, developmental interventions, rehabilitation, behavioral support, and coordinated multidisciplinary care. Future research should prioritize disease-modifying therapies and personalized strategies aimed at addressing both epileptic and non-epileptic manifestations, ultimately improving functional outcomes and quality of life for individuals with DEEs and their families.

items.title: From missed diagnosis to lifelong survivorship: a precision oncology roadmap for equity in pediatric and AYA cancer care.
items.authors: Obeagu EI.

sections.text: Cancer in children, adolescents, and young adults (AYA) remains a global health challenge, with disparities in survival and quality of life between high-resource and low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). These disparities arise across the cancer continuum, including delayed recognition, inadequate diagnostic capacity, fragmented referral pathways, treatment abandonment, limited supportive care, unequal access to molecular diagnostics, and insufficient survivorship services. Precision oncology provides an opportunity to address these challenges, but its equity potential extends beyond genomic sequencing and targeted therapies. This narrative review examines an integrated precision oncology continuum encompassing early recognition, diagnostic and pathological accuracy, molecular characterization, risk stratification, precision treatment, response monitoring, supportive care, and lifelong survivorship. Evidence from LMIC settings is used to illustrate diagnostic delay, referral barriers, treatment abandonment, health-system limitations, and outcome disparities without attempting an exhaustive country comparison. The review proposes a tiered, equity-centered framework in which foundational cancer services are strengthened alongside progressively accessible molecular and digital technologies. Regional referral networks, patient navigation, tele-oncology, pathology and laboratory networks, targeted molecular testing, multidisciplinary care, survivorship planning, and longitudinal cancer registries are emphasized as practical components. For AYA patients, fertility, reproductive health, mental health, education, employment, and transition between pediatric and adult services are incorporated into precision care. Ultimately, equitable precision oncology should connect biological precision with health-system precision, ensuring that every young person can receive timely diagnosis, appropriate treatment, continuous monitoring, and lifelong survivorship support.

items.title: Style transfer mapping with ensemble learning for cross-subject EEG-based neuropsychiatric disease recognition.
items.authors: Ding X, Guo Y, Ge S, Yang S, Su J, Xu M, Wang X, Chang H.

sections.text: Cross-subject electroencephalogram (EEG) recognition remains a fundamental challenge because large inter-subject variability causes severe distribution shifts that substantially degrade the generalization ability of existing learning models. Most existing transfer learning methods attempt to align global feature distributions but often overlook subject-specific structural variations, resulting in unstable adaptation under limited calibration data. To address this problem, we propose a Prototype-Consistent Style Transfer Mapping (PC-STM) framework for cross-subject neuropsychiatric disease recognition. Unlike conventional domain adaptation methods, the proposed framework models subject discrepancy as a prototype-guided style transformation that explicitly aligns target representations with class-consistent source prototypes while preserving discriminative structures. Specifically, a multi-source prototype construction strategy is introduced to characterize representative class distributions, followed by a confidence-aware transductive semi-supervised style transfer module that iteratively refines transformation parameters using labeled calibration samples and unlabeled evaluation samples. Furthermore, a reliability-aware ensemble learning strategy dynamically aggregates multiple subject-specific classifiers according to their calibration consistency, thereby improving robustness against heterogeneous subject distributions. Experiments on two public EEG datasets covering major depressive disorder and Parkinson's disease show stable performance under the evaluated leave-one-pair-out protocol. The calibration labels are inherited from the public dataset cohorts or task conditions, and the study does not constitute prospective clinical diagnostic validation. Beyond the evaluated EEG tasks, prototype-guided style transfer may provide a basis for future investigation of other limited-supervision recognition problems.

items.title: Participant experiences and recommendations for psychedelic clinical trials and future treatment delivery: a qualitative study with experts by experience from the Psychedelic Participant Advocacy Network.
items.authors: Seynaeve M, Schneider L, Roullier I, Lazenby K, Lilley C, Lobo S, Ermakova AO, Wells H, Cleare A, Rucker J.

sections.text: While psychedelic treatments for difficult-to-treat mental health conditions are advancing, participant perspectives remain under-explored. This study examined former participants' experiences across recruitment, preparation, dosing, integration and study ending, and generated recommendations for future trials and treatment delivery. This qualitative descriptive study, informed by reflexive thematic analysis, included four Psychedelic Participant Advocacy Network (PsyPAN) members who were former psychedelic-trial participants. They completed three remote focus groups on recruitment and screening, preparation and dosing, and post-dose integration and the post-study period. Three had joined treatment-resistant depression studies involving psilocybin or N,N-dimethyltryptamine; one had joined a psilocybin study for an eating disorder. items.title: Associations between the "Double Reduction" policy and physical activity and overweight/obesity among Chinese school-aged children: a quasi-experimental difference-in-differences analysis.
items.authors: Yu W, Zhang B.

sections.text: In July 2021, China implemented the "Double Reduction" policy to ease homework burden and curb off-campus tutoring for students in compulsory education. The policy has been evaluated mainly for academic and mental health outcomes; whether it coincided with changes in physical activity and weight status is unclear. This study used the policy as a natural experiment to examine associations between the Double Reduction policy, moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), and overweight/obesity among Chinese school-aged children. We analyzed the 2018, 2020, and 2022 waves of the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS) in a quasi-experimental difference-in-differences (DiD) design. At each wave, students enrolled in compulsory education (grades 1-9) formed the treatment group and senior high school students (grades 10-12), who were not covered by the policy, formed the comparison group. The analytical sample comprised 4,237 students contributing 10,799 person-wave observations. Outcomes were self-reported weekly MVPA minutes and overweight/obesity defined by age- and sex-specific body mass index z-scores (WHO 2007 reference). Event-study specifications, propensity-score weighting, longitudinal survey weights, and placebo tests assessed the stability of the estimates. The policy was associated with 43.1 additional MVPA minutes per week (95% CI: 33.8-52.3; p < 0.001) and a 3.9 percentage-point reduction in overweight/obesity (95% CI: -7.2 to -0.6; p = 0.022) among compulsory education students relative to the comparison group. Estimates were larger among primary school students and among children whose parents had lower educational attainment. The 2018 pre-policy interaction was small and not statistically significant for either outcome, although two pre-policy waves offer limited power for testing pre-trends. Estimates were similar under balanced-panel, propensity-score-weighted, survey-weighted, and placebo specifications. The Double Reduction policy coincided with measurable improvements in physical activity and weight status among Chinese school-aged children. Education policies that relieve academic burden may carry collateral public health benefits and deserve explicit consideration in child health strategies.

items.title: Identity development and the transition to adulthood under polycrisis: a one-year longitudinal study of emerging adults.
items.authors: Wendołowska A, Sitnik-Warchulska K, Kałwak W, Gruszka A, Czyżowska D, Izydorczyk B.

sections.text: Contemporary emerging adults are navigating the transition to adulthood under conditions of prolonged societal uncertainty associated with multiple concurrent global crises. Although psychological stress has been extensively linked to poorer mental health, considerably less is known about its prospective associations with identity development and adulthood attainment. This longitudinal study examined whether baseline psychological stress burden prospectively predicted identity development, adulthood attainment, and resilience-related resources over 1 year, and whether baseline resilience-related resources prospectively predicted identity and adulthood attainment independently of stress burden. Data were drawn from a nationwide longitudinal panel of 831 Polish emerging adults (18-29 years) assessed at two time points separated by 1 year. Psychological stress burden was modelled as a latent factor indicated by perceived stress, adjustment-disorder symptoms, and polycrisis-related adjustment difficulties. Identity development was assessed using the five-dimensional model of identity formation, alongside measures of resilience-related resources and subjective and objective adulthood. Longitudinal hypotheses were examined using autoregressive structural equation models controlling for baseline levels of the respective outcomes and relevant sociodemographic covariates. Subjective adulthood was modelled as a binary outcome using probit structural equation modelling. All developmental outcomes showed significant rank-order stability across the follow-up period, while mean-level changes were generally small. Higher baseline psychological stress burden prospectively predicted greater ruminative exploration, lower commitment making, and lower identification with commitment, but was not significantly associated with exploration in breadth, exploration in depth, resilience-related resources, objective adulthood, or subjective adulthood. Higher baseline resilience-related resources prospectively predicted greater exploration in breadth, commitment making, exploration in depth, and identification with commitment, independently of baseline psychological stress burden, but did not significantly predict ruminative exploration, objective or subjective adulthood. Psychological stress burden and resilience-related resources showed distinct prospective associations with identity development, whereas neither significantly predicted objective or subjective adulthood after accounting for baseline levels and covariates. Higher psychological stress burden was associated with greater ruminative exploration and weaker commitment-related processes, whereas resilience-related resources were associated with both adaptive exploration and commitment processes. These findings suggest that, over the one-year interval examined, prospective associations with psychological stress burden and resilience-related resources were concentrated primarily within identity development rather than broader adulthood attainment. Longer multiwave studies are needed to determine how these associations unfold across the transition to adulthood.

items.title: The Moderating Role of Social Support in the Relationship Between Diabetes Distress and Psychological Well-Being Among Older Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Study Protocol.
items.authors: Imani E, Roosta-Ye Abkenar M.

sections.heading: Background and aims
sections.text: Type 2 diabetes imposes a considerable psychological burden on older adults, including elevated diabetes distress and diminished psychological well-being. Social support may buffer the harmful mental-health effects of chronic disease-related stress, yet whether it moderates the link between diabetes distress and psychological well-being remains rarely examined among older Iranian adults with type 2 diabetes. This protocol aims to determine the moderating role of social support in that relationship in this population.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This descriptive-analytic cross-sectional protocol will recruit 300 adults aged 60 years or above with type 2 diabetes from the Bandar Abbas Diabetes Clinic through simple random sampling from the clinic electronic registry. Trained interviewers will administer a demographic and clinical form, the age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index, the PAID-5 (diabetes distress), the MSSS-5 (social support), and the WHO-5 Well-Being Index in person or by telephone using identical structured interviews. Hierarchical multiple regression will test the diabetes distress by social support interaction on WHO-5 scores, in an unadjusted model and a model adjusted for a pre-specified demographic and clinical covariate set, with heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors, bootstrapped confidence intervals, and simple-slopes and Johnson-Neyman probing. Missing data will be handled with multiple imputation. Analyses will use IBM SPSS Statistics version 28 with two-sided tests at α  = 0.05.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: As a protocol, no empirical results are reported. The completed study will yield estimates of diabetes distress, social support, and psychological well-being levels, their bivariate associations, and the moderation effect with appropriate uncertainty quantification.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The findings are expected to provide a scientific basis for nursing and psychosocial interventions that strengthen social support networks to protect the psychological well-being of older adults with type 2 diabetes. Ethical approval has been obtained (IR.HUMS.REC.1405.013); written or audio-recorded verbal informed consent will be obtained from all participants.

items.title: Inpatient Dementia Mental Health Care in the UK: A National Mapping Survey of Ward Provision and Family Carer Involvement.
items.authors: Bean N, Underwood BR, Dunn R, Gillam J, Watson F, Wolverson E.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: Inpatient mental health wards provide specialist care for people with dementia experiencing acute behavioural disturbance. The scale and configuration of this provision, and how these services involve family carers, have not previously been described at a national level. This study aimed to map ward provision across the UK and characterise existing policies and practices related to carer involvement.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A national cross-sectional online mapping survey was conducted across mental health wards providing care for people with dementia in the UK. Wards were identified through a structured multi-source search strategy. The survey captured ward characteristics, patient profile, staffing and approaches to carer involvement. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively; Fisher's exact test was used to examine associations between categorical variables.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: 209 wards comprising over 3100 beds across 80 provider organisations were identified. 63 wards (30.1%) participated, reporting 801 patients. Most patients were detained under mental health or capacity legislation (87.8%) and few were expected to return home (14.8%). While all wards reported involving carers in clinical decision-making, 44.4% indicated carers did not routinely attend MDT meetings and 30.2% did not routinely share care plans. Staff training in carer engagement was a consistent marker of greater carer involvement across multiple measures.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This survey provides the first national picture of inpatient dementia mental health care in the UK, revealing a service under considerable pressure and a consistent gap between the basic infrastructure for carer involvement and its meaningful integration into clinical practice. Staff training in carer engagement was strongly associated with greater carer involvement, pointing to an actionable route to improvement.

items.title: The Impact of 12-Hour Versus 8-Hour Shifts on Intensive Care Unit Nurses' Physical and Mental Well-Being and Job Satisfaction: A Systematic Review.
items.authors: Othman A, Najm D, Zimbudzi E.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Twelve-hour shifts have been widely implemented in intensive care units (ICUs), where nurses work in high-acuity environments requiring sustained clinical attention. However, evidence regarding the impact of shift length on ICU nurses' physical health, mental well-being, job satisfaction and patient-care outcomes remains limited and inconsistent.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To investigate the impact of 12-h compared with 8-h shifts on ICU nurses' physical health, well-being and job satisfaction.

sections.heading: Design
sections.text: This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines and was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251021178).

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A systematic search of CINAHL, Ovid MEDLINE and Embase was conducted in February 2025 and updated in June 2026. Additional searches of Scopus and Web of Science were undertaken in June 2026. Eligible studies included ICU nurses and compared 12-h with 8-h shifts. Risk of bias and methodological quality were assessed using design-specific Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools and the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach. Findings were synthesised narratively due to the heterogeneity of the included studies.

sections.heading: Result
sections.text: Of 815 records identified, five studies met the inclusion criteria. Findings on fatigue, sleep and burnout were inconclusive across studies. Twelve-hour shifts were generally associated with greater roster satisfaction, flexibility and work-life balance, while evidence for sick leave was limited or mixed.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Evidence did not consistently favour either 12- or 8-h shifts for ICU nurses, with low to very low certainty of evidence. Shift duration should therefore be considered alongside overall roster design, staffing needs and nurses' well-being when planning ICU schedules.

sections.heading: Implications for nursing management
sections.text: Nurse managers should avoid a one-size-fits-all approach to shift duration, as evidence does not clearly favour 12- or 8-h shifts. Shift-length decisions should consider roster design, staffing needs, workload, recovery time and nurses' preferences. Managers should also monitor staff well-being, satisfaction, absenteeism, retention and patient-care outcomes when reviewing shift patterns. Given the low certainty of evidence, ongoing local evaluation is essential to ensure rosters support workforce sustainability and safe, high-quality care.

items.title: Correlations between Surface Temperature and Atmospheric CO_2 Emissions with Health-Related Factors in WANA: An Ecological Study.
items.authors: Soori H, Ghasempour A.
items.journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran

sections.text: Climate change impacts public health. This study aims to examine climate change-related diseases in the West Asia and North Africa (WANA) region, comparing health outcomes with global data. This study employed a secondary data analysis with an ecological design, focusing on climate change-related diseases and their associated health outcomes in 21 countries across WANA from 1990 to 2023. Data were sourced from reputable organizations and cleaned for inconsistencies. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the data, while correlation and regression analyses assessed the relationships between climate variables and health outcomes, utilizing SPSS version 22 for statistical analysis. The WANA region-which accounts for about 10% of the world's population-continues to warm with higher atmospheric CO2, impacting health outcomes. The annual heat-related mortality rate averages 1.95 per 100,000, indicating a slight decrease. Mental health indicators show a -1.17% change, while anxiety has surged by 21.70%. Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALYs) have declined by 23.6%, suggesting a reduced overall disease burden in this region. Temperature is the main driver of heat-mortality risk: a 1°C increase raises heat-mortality odds by 57%. A 1% rise in CO2 increases asthma odds by 3%, a statistically significant, public-health-relevant effect. The region differs notably from the global average and from countries with minimal climate impact. The study advocates a strategy addressing climate-related mental health impacts through environmental policy, public health, and mental-health support, with recommendations to improve data collection, target vulnerable groups, develop heat action plans, and foster regional partnerships.

items.title: Longitudinal Changes in Bullying, Self-Esteem, and Emotional Intelligence Following a Mental Health Nursing-Led Emotional Education Program in Primary School Children.
items.authors: Barba-Muñoz M, Molés-Julio MP, Zafra-Agea JA.

sections.heading: Aim
sections.text: To examine longitudinal changes in bullying involvement, self-esteem, and perceived emotional intelligence following participation in a mental health nursing-led emotional education programme among primary school children.

sections.heading: Design
sections.text: Multicentre, longitudinal, non-randomized, uncontrolled quasi-experimental pretest-posttest study.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The study was conducted in 5 public primary schools in Madrid, Spain. A total of 507 students in fourth to sixth grade completed baseline assessment and 345 completed follow-up. The programme included five student sessions, 2 parent sessions, and one teacher session. Bullying involvement, self-esteem, and perceived emotional intelligence were assessed using self-report instruments. Pretest-posttest analyses used valid matched observations for each outcome, complemented by exploratory posttest association analyses.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Bullying involvement decreased from pretest to posttest. No clear pretest-posttest changes were observed in self-esteem, emotional attention, emotional clarity, or emotional repair. At posttest, higher self-esteem, emotional clarity, and emotional repair were inversely associated with bullying involvement. These concurrent associations were interpreted as non-causal.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Participation in the programme was followed by reduced bullying involvement, while self-esteem and perceived emotional intelligence remained broadly stable. The uncontrolled design precludes causal attribution.

sections.heading: Implications for the profession and/or patient care
sections.text: School nurses and mental health nurses may contribute to bullying prevention through health education, early identification of psychosocial vulnerability, emotional support, and coordination with families and teachers.

sections.heading: Impact
sections.text: The study addresses nursing involvement in school-based bullying prevention. Bullying involvement decreased, while other psychosocial outcomes remained stable. The findings may inform nursing practice and future controlled evaluations in primary schools.

sections.heading: Reporting method
sections.text: Reporting was guided by the Transparent Reporting of Evaluations with Nonrandomized Designs statement.

sections.heading: No patient or public contribution
sections.text: Students, parents, and teachers participated in the intervention and data collection but were not involved in study design, analysis, interpretation, or manuscript preparation.

The study addresses nursing involvement in school-based bullying prevention. Bullying involvement decreased, while other psychosocial outcomes remained stable. The findings may inform nursing practice and future controlled evaluations in primary schools.

Reporting was guided by the Transparent Reporting of Evaluations with Nonrandomized Designs statement.

Students, parents, and teachers participated in the intervention and data collection but were not involved in study design, analysis, interpretation, or manuscript preparation.

items.title: Implementing a mental fitness workshop in a Canadian Practical Nursing Program: A qualitative descriptive study.
items.authors: Frost L, Borras J, Dysangco A, Carine Makwaira V.

sections.text: Nursing students experience high levels of stress that can negatively affect mental health and well-being. This study explored practical nursing students' perceptions of the acceptability and perceived value of a brief mental fitness workshop integrated into nursing education. Two sessions from a condensed version of the Mastering My Mental Fitness for Nurses program were embedded within a fourth‑semester laboratory course. A qualitative descriptive design was used, drawing on reflexive thematic analysis of semi‑structured interviews (n = 5) and free‑text post‑session feedback forms (n = 49). Participants reported enhanced awareness of stress and burnout, reframed self‑care as a professional responsibility, and valued opportunities for peer connection through small‑group discussions. Students recommended earlier and more frequent integration within the curriculum and greater flexibility in delivery. While the findings reflect short‑term perceptions rather than clinical outcomes, the workshops were perceived as feasible and acceptable, with implications for mental health promotion and burnout prevention among nursing students. Future research should examine impact using validated mental health and well-being measures.

items.title: Leveraging Primary Care Resources Through Quality Improvement to Increase Follow-up After Mental Health Emergency Department Visits.
items.authors: Krantz LB, Vaughn SE, McClure JM, Walters J, Gehring E, Mahan A, Spitznagel J, Reisman T, Brinkman WB.

sections.text: Timely follow-up after mental behavioral health (MBH) crises can improve health outcomes; moreover, it is a national quality metric. We aimed to improve the completion of 7-day follow-up after emergency department (ED) discharge for youth with an MBH concern from 28.7% of discharges to 50.0% within 12 months. We used quality improvement methods from November 1, 2024, to October 31, 2025, across 3 primary care sites and 2 ED sites. Baseline data, literature reviews, and lived experience identified key drivers and failure modes. We developed 2 interventions: (1) direct phone outreach after discharge and (2) increased access in pediatric primary care (PPC). The primary outcome measure was the percentage of ED MBH discharges with a completed follow-up appointment within 7 days of discharge. Process measures included the percentage of patients who received a postdischarge outreach call and who followed up within PPC. The balancing measure was return ED MBH visits within 30 days. The mean follow-up percentage increased from 28.7% (n = 258) to 40.3% (n = 334). Follow-up for Medicaid-insured patients increased from 24% to 35% and remained stable for commercially insured patients (42%), decreasing our equity gap by 11%. Outreach calls occurred following 52.4% of discharges. Follow-up visits within PPC increased from 3.5% of discharges to 10.7% of discharges. There was no change in return ED visits within 30 days of ED discharge. Increasing access to pediatric primary care and implementing timely postdischarge follow-up calls can improve follow-up within a large healthcare system for patients discharged from the ED for MBH concerns.

items.title: Temporal Trends and Social Inequalities in Adverse Childhood Experiences Among Children in the United States, 2016-2023.
items.authors: Uddin J, Hossin MZ, Sadid SAM, Smith C, Deepchand D, Hajizadeh M.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: Temporal changes in specific adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) and related inequalities remain unclear. We examined trends and social inequalities in age-standardized ACE prevalence among US children from 2016 through 2023.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Data were drawn from the National Survey of Children's Health (n = 309 425; ages 0-17 y). Age-standardized prevalence was estimated for 9 ACEs and 2 summary measures (any ACE and ≥4 ACEs). Differences in ACE prevalence were examined across key social and demographic characteristics, including children's sex, race and ethnicity, parental nativity, parental education, and family income.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: From 2016 through 2023, the prevalence of financial hardship (from 25.3% to 13.8%), parental divorce (from 24.5% to 20.7%), parental imprisonment (from 7.9% to 5.6%), any ACE (from 46.0% to 37.4%), and ≥4 ACEs (from 6.1% to 4.8%) showed statistically significant declines (all P for trend < .001). In contrast, the prevalence of parental mental illness (from 7.8% to 8.3%) and race and ethnicity-related discrimination (ranging from 3.6% to 4.4%) increased modestly. Black children consistently had higher ACE prevalence than non-Hispanic White children, particularly for discrimination (ranging from 9.1% to 14.9%), financial hardship (from 17.5% to 36.2%), and parental imprisonment (from 9.4% to 15.8%) during 2016-2023. Racial and ethnic and nativity gaps in parental imprisonment and financial hardship narrowed over time, although substantial differences remained. Across all years, children from lower-income and lower-education families consistently experienced higher ACE prevalence than their more advantaged counterparts.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Despite modest reductions in some ACEs, social differences in ACEs persisted over time. Findings highlight the continued concentration of ACEs among socioeconomically disadvantaged children, underscoring the need for structural and policy interventions targeting upstream social determinants.

items.title: No association between body dissatisfaction and attentional bias towards lower-weight bodies in a non-clinical sample of women: an eye-tracking study.
items.authors: Crisp C, Jin Y, Nealon MS, Low H, Heron J, Gilchrist ID, Penton-Voak I, Bould H.

sections.text: Body dissatisfaction is a key risk factor for psychiatric illnesses and is a modifiable target. Previous gaze-tracking research suggests that body dissatisfaction is related to greater attentional bias towards lower-weight bodies. Here, we aimed to partially replicate and extend previous work to verify this association by using realistic body stimuli and a validated scale of body dissatisfaction. Sixty, mostly young, women from the general population underwent eye-tracking while viewing picture pairs of women's bodies morphed to lower and higher weights. Attentional bias was measured as percentage fixation duration, fixation count and first fixations on lower-weight compared to higher-weight bodies. There was weak evidence that all women fixated for longer on lower-weight bodies, and that participants with higher body dissatisfaction spent less time fixating on lower-weight bodies, contrary to our hypotheses and to previous findings, but this effect was not robust to adjustment for age and body mass index. This lack of replication suggests this association is not robust in non-clinical populations. Instead, an overall bias towards lower-weight bodies could contribute to higher levels of body dissatisfaction and risk of mental health problems in younger women. Future studies measuring attentional biases in realistic settings and in clinical populations with eating disorder symptoms are needed.

items.title: Beyond Static Representations: Learning Electroencephalogram Spatiotemporal Dynamics for Enhanced Emotion Recognition.
items.authors: Liu K, Zhu W, Xu R, Wang W, Yu Z, Wu W.

sections.text: Electroencephalogram (EEG)-based emotion recognition plays a pivotal role in brain-computer interfaces and mental health monitoring. However, conventional approaches often neglect the intrinsic spatial correlations among EEG channels and fail to effectively model both global temporal dependencies and the continuity of neural oscillations. To overcome these challenges, we propose the Dynamic Spatial Embedding and Temporal Attention Mamba (DSE-TAM) framework. Our Dynamic Spatial Embedding (DSE) module leverages graph convolutional networks to dynamically capture inter-channel relationships, preserving spatial coherence in EEG representations. Subsequently, the Temporal Attention Mamba module integrates self-attention with state-space models to jointly optimize long-range temporal dependencies and smooth transition dynamics. Extensive experiments on 2 public benchmarks (DEAP and DREAMER) and an in-house CEED dataset demonstrate that DSE-TAM surpasses state-of-the-art methods, achieving accuracies of 79.75% (arousal) and 78.27% (valence) on DEAP, 80.55% (arousal) and 83.91% (valence) on DREAMER, and 73.75% (3-class) on CEED. These results validate the framework's efficacy in advancing EEG-based emotion decoding for brain-computer interfaces. The source code is available at https://github.com/Raizeroko/DSE-TAM.

items.title: Mishel theory-based perioperative nursing after trabeculectomy for primary glaucoma: effects on illness uncertainty, self-management, and quality of life.
items.authors: Ding QY, Li C, Yin XM.

sections.text: To evaluate the effects of a perioperative nursing intervention based on Mishel's Uncertainty in Illness Theory in patients with primary glaucoma undergoing trabeculectomy. This single-center, two-arm, parallel-group randomized controlled study enrolled 198 patients undergoing first trabeculectomy at The First Affiliated Hospital of Suzhou University between February 2024 and December 2025. Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 to routine perioperative ophthalmic nursing or routine care plus a structured Mishel theory-based nursing intervention. Assessments were conducted 1 day before surgery (T0), at discharge (T1), and at 1 month (T2) and 3 months (T3) after surgery. The primary outcome was illness uncertainty measured using the Mishel Uncertainty in Illness Scale. Secondary outcomes included psychological status, discharge readiness, self-management, medication adherence, sleep quality, vision-related quality of life, satisfaction with nursing care, postoperative ophthalmic outcomes, and complications. All randomized participants completed follow-up and were analyzed according to their assigned groups. After Holm adjustment, the intervention group had lower illness-uncertainty scores at T1, T2, and T3; lower anxiety scores at T1 and T3 and lower depression scores at T2 and T3; higher discharge-readiness and satisfaction-with-nursing-care at T1; higher self-management and medication-adherence scores and lower sleep-quality scores at T2 and T3; and lower GQL-15 scores at T3. At T3, the model-estimated between-group differences were -8.13 points for illness uncertainty (95% CI, -10.74 to -5.53), 5.64 points for self-management (95% CI, 4.08-7.19), 6.05 points for medication adherence (95% CI, 2.98-9.12), and -3.71 points for GQL-15 (95% CI, -5.41 to -2.00). At discharge, the between-group difference in discharge readiness was 1.23 points (95% CI, 0.99-1.47). No statistically significant between-group differences were detected in postoperative intraocular-pressure trajectories, visual-acuity recovery, medication-free status, postoperative procedures, or complications within 3 months. In this single-center randomized study, Mishel theory-based perioperative nursing was associated with greater improvements in illness uncertainty and several psychological, behavioral, and recovery-related patient-reported outcomes after trabeculectomy. No statistically significant differences were detected in short-term objective ophthalmic outcomes or postoperative complications.

items.title: Projecting the real through active inference: a unified model of reality construction from neuronal dynamics to social consensus a neuroscientific framework for psychopathology.
items.authors: G P, P P.

sections.text: How does the brain transform a chaotic stream of sensory signals into a stable, shared experience of reality? This theoretical paper proposes that the brain does not passively receive the world, but actively projects it - it continuously generates predictions about sensory inputs and updates its internal model when predictions fail, a process formally described by the free energy principle and active inference. We argue that this process can be understood through an analogy with quantum decoherence - the collapse of multiple possibilities into a single actuality. By integrating insights from this analogy with active inference, we show how the brain resolves sensory uncertainty into a coherent projection of reality. A central question we address is whether projecting reality changes it. We argue that it does: a strong, coherent projection reduces uncertainty, while a weak or fragmented one amplifies prediction errors, and a distorted one - diverging from social consensus - leads to alternative realities that resist correction. This projection operates in discrete, rhythmic cycles governed by brain waves and is fine-tuned by neurochemicals that determine how much we "trust" our predictions versus new sensory data. The Default Mode Network - the brain's inner "sea" of self-awareness, memories, and context - acts as a central hub that integrates and updates these projections. Crucially, individual projections are stabilized into a shared, "solid" reality through social interaction, language, and culture - a process we call collective active inference. Within this framework, psychiatric disorders are understood as disorders of projection - distortions in how the brain generates and stabilizes its model of reality. This perspective reverses the traditional explanatory gradient: psychopathology is not merely a sensory or chemical problem, but a fundamental disruption of the brain's capacity to project a coherent world. This unifying framework offers a new foundation for both pharmacological and psychotherapeutic interventions, grounding them in a common computational logic.

items.title: Verbal de-escalation techniques for the prevention and management of workplace violence in healthcare: a systematic review.
items.authors: Seiyad H, Nimako J, Singh B, Lyver B, Villavicencio S, Anderson M, Whiteside R, Shannon J, Chandler A, Vaughan T, Toppings M, Styra R, Schulz-Quach C.

sections.text: Workplace violence (WPV) remains a significant and escalating challenge across healthcare settings, threatening the safety, well-being, and retention of frontline healthcare professionals (HCPs). Verbal de-escalation is widely promoted as a first-line strategy to prevent or manage aggressive patient behavior. However, the scope, implementation, and effectiveness of these techniques have not been consistently synthesized. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Studies were eligible if they examined verbal de-escalation as a primary strategy for preventing or managing WPV in healthcare settings, including hospitals, emergency departments, psychiatric units, long-term care, and outpatient clinics. All study designs were considered, including empirical research and structured descriptive guidance relevant to clinical practice. Searches were conducted in Ovid MEDLINE ALL, Embase, Emcare, PsycINFO, and CINAHL from database inception, with results downloaded on August 29, 2024, and updated on January 30, 2026. Of 15,987 records identified, 9,096 were screened following duplicate removal, 446 underwent full-text review, and 36 studies met inclusion criteria. Methodological quality was appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Substantial heterogeneity was observed in how verbal de-escalation was defined, delivered, and evaluated. Intervention studies commonly assessed structured training programs delivered through didactic sessions, interactive workshops, simulation-based education, technology-enhanced learning, or clinical unit-based training. These studies frequently reported improvements in staff knowledge, confidence, and preparedness to manage aggression. Observational and descriptive studies emphasized communication behaviors used during escalated encounters and highlighted recurring strategies, such as empathetic listening, calm verbal tone, validation, and collaborative problem-solving. Outcome measures varied considerably across studies, limiting direct comparison. Verbal de-escalation represents a central component of WPV prevention in healthcare, yet implementation approaches and evaluation methods remain inconsistent. The evidence suggests associations with improved clinician confidence, reduced patient agitation, and enhanced perceptions of safety. Healthcare organizations can use these findings to strengthen training curricula, integrate de-escalation within broader safety frameworks, and support sustainable workforce protection strategies. OSF, identifier https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/S7QD9.

items.title: Undercounting mental health-related impairments and disability in US federal surveys.
items.authors: Qu A, Johnston KJ, Stein BD, Druss BG, Wen H.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: US federal surveys use the ACS Six Questions (ACS-6) and Washington Group Short Set on Functioning (WG-SS) to inform disability-related policy and resource allocation. The ACS-6 is used more broadly in general household and health surveys, and the WG-SS is primarily used in health surveys. However, these surveys largely focus on physical function and may miss psychosocial impairments experienced by populations with mental health conditions.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We used data from 2017-2019 and 2022-2024 of the National Survey on Drug Use and Health, which assesses functional impairment attributable to mental health using the World Health Organization Disability Assessment Schedule (WHODAS). We examined overall and racial/ethnic differences in undercounting of mental health-related disabilities in the ACS-6 and WG-SS scales.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among adults with serious mental illness (SMI), the ACS-6 failed to identify 39.5% as having disability, and the WG-SS failed to identify 12.8%. Individuals who reported difficulty socializing had the lowest identification rate across WHODAS domains. Relative to non-Hispanic White individuals, the disability measures identified fewer non-Hispanic Black individuals and non-Hispanic Asian/Pacific Islander individuals.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: This undercounting may limit resources for individuals with mental health-related disabilities. Researchers and policymakers should revise disability questions to capture social impairments, fluctuating mental health symptoms, and cultural influences.

items.title: Somatotopic functional connectivity gradients in the monkey and human striatum.
items.authors: Goda N, Chiken S, Koketsu D, Nambu A, Fukunaga M.

sections.text: Understanding the topographic and functional organization of the striatum-a key brain structure involved in motor control, learning, and cognition-is crucial for elucidating the pathophysiology of the neurological and psychiatric disorders associated to it, and for developing targeted therapies. While recent magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies in humans and non-human primates have noninvasively characterized the brain-wide connectivity patterns of the striatum, its detailed somatotopic organization and the homology across species remains to be fully elucidated. We aimed to comprehensively characterize the somatotopic organization of the striatum in macaque monkeys based on functional connectivity patterns, and to assess the extent of homology or divergence of this organization between macaque monkeys and humans. Resting-state functional connectivity data were obtained from 11 anesthetized macaques using an ultra-high-field 7-tesla MRI scanner. Using two complementary approaches-seed-based analysis and connectopic mapping-we successfully delineated a distinct, regular volumetric somatotopic map within the macaque posterior putamen, a motor-related subregion of the striatum. This map exhibited a gradient encompassing the lower limb, trunk, upper limb, and face representations, predominantly oriented along the dorsal-ventral axis. The somatotopic gradient identified in macaques demonstrated a remarkable similarity with the corresponding gradient in the human posterior putamen, characterized using a publicly available resting-state functional MRI dataset. Furthermore, cross-species decoding analysis revealed that the somatotopy of the human posterior putamen could be accurately predicted using the anatomically aligned macaque somatotopic map obtained in this study as reference. In addition to this shared gradient organization, our seed-based analyses suggested non-gradient-like features in the human posterior putamen. These findings offer compelling evidence for the high evolutionary conservation of the major topographic organization in the primate posterior putamen, while pointing to species-specific divergence.

items.title: ANCHOR: Communication Partner Training for Maintaining Friendships After Aphasia.
items.authors: Azios JH, Archer B, Douglas NF, Strong KA, Eller MA, Silverman M, Simmons-Mackie N, Worrall L.
items.journal: International journal of language & communication disorders

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Aphasia significantly disrupts social relationships, with friendship loss occurring early after stroke and continuing into chronic stages. Despite friendships being prioritised by people with aphasia and families, they rarely receive explicit focus in rehabilitation. Communication partner training is an intervention with potential to keep friendship bonds strong after aphasia.

sections.heading: Aims
sections.text: This paper describes the development of ANCHOR (Aphasia: Nurturing Connection, Honoring Ongoing Relationships), a communication partner training intervention protoype designed specifically for people with aphasia and their pre-existing friends-and the foundational elements of ANCHOR and how they informed its design and components, and then situates ANCHOR within the broader communication partner training literature with attention to partner type, candidacy and real-world delivery in service settings.

sections.heading: Main contribution
sections.text: ANCHOR represents the first communication partner training intervention explicitly targeting friendship maintenance after aphasia. Development was grounded in a systematic research progression including lived experience research, relational competence theory and the behaviour change wheel, and a planned cycle of refinement across a two-year development period. Key distinguishing features include a hybrid delivery model that combines self-paced digital modules with in-person coaching sessions, universal 'talking tools' accessible to friends with minimal aphasia knowledge, first-year post-stroke timing to prevent relationship deterioration, and explicit attention to implementation barriers.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: By grounding communication partner training design in lived experience, relationship theory and implementation science, ANCHOR is designed as a comprehensive, implementable approach to sustaining friendships after aphasia, thereby addressing a critical gap in post-stroke rehabilitation with potential to reduce social isolation and support mental health. ANCHOR is an intervention prototype and its core functions, forms and implementation supports will be refined as feasibility and trial data accrue.

sections.heading: What this paper adds
sections.text: What is already known on this subject Aphasia greatly impacts the ability for people to maintain a strong social network. People with aphasia often lose most of their pre-stroke friends early in the recovery journey. Friends of people with aphasia need access to interventions that can help them understand aphasia and its impact on communication. What this study adds to the existing knowledge We developed a communication partner training program called ANCHOR based upon lived experience research involving people with aphasia and their friends and theories and relationship maintenance and behaviour change. ANCHOR is different than other communication partner training programs which target family members or healthcare providers in that it is limited to three face-to-face sessions, includes a self-guided digital component, and focuses on a standard package of communication strategies. What are the potential clinical implications of the study? ANCHOR continues to be refined and evaluated. It is our hope that ANCHOR will be a clinically feasible and person-centered communication partner training program that is effective in improving communication and relationships for people with aphasia and their friends.

items.title: Xenocortical mice: what can we learn, and how should this research progress?
items.authors: Farahany N, Seth AK.
items.journal: Journal of law and the biosciences

sections.text: A new study by researchers at Stanford University describes the development of 'xenocortical mice': mice with a cortex comprised almost entirely of human-derived neurons. Their groundbreaking research has the potential to enable medical breakthroughs for a range of neurological and psychiatric disorders. The researchers offer detailed analysis of the neurophysiological and behavioral properties of these chimeric mice, comparing them with both wild-type control mice, and 'apallial' mice lacking most of their cortex. Here, we outline some key findings from the study and ask what these findings tell us about the capacity for consciousness in these mice, as well as their potential for human-like properties of cognition or conscious experience. Based on this discussion, we summarize the ethical and regulatory landscape relevant to chimeric animals and lay out an ethically-informed research roadmap to guide future research in this important area.

items.title: Mental Health and Addiction Care Professionals' Views on Artificial Intelligence Integration in Oman: A Descriptive Qualitative Study.
items.authors: Al-Abri KR, Al Saadi AA, Al Rashdi AY, Al Nasseri JM, Al Mashaykhi AK, Al Maqbali AO, Alharrasi SS.

sections.heading: Aim
sections.text: To explore mental health and addiction care professionals' views on integrating artificial intelligence into clinical practice at a tertiary psychiatric hospital.

sections.heading: Design
sections.text: A qualitative descriptive study.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Purposive sampling recruited 17 nurses, psychiatrists, psychologists, and social workers. Face-to-face semi-structured interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, translated from Arabic into English, and analysed through codebook-based thematic analysis informed by Braun and Clarke's six phases.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Four themes were identified: variable familiarity with artificial intelligence (AI); actual experience with artificial intelligence and non-artificial-intelligence digital technologies, with telemedicine and electronic health records more common than AI-specific tools; anticipated benefits involving efficiency, clinical decision support, communication, data management, and service access; and anticipated barriers concerning infrastructure, resources, training, clinical suitability, therapeutic relationships, and ethics.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Participants were cautiously optimistic but had limited direct clinical experience and sometimes conflated AI with other digital technologies. Safe implementation requires a shared understanding of AI, reliable infrastructure, role-specific education, ethical governance, accountable human oversight, and protection of therapeutic relationships.

sections.heading: Patient or public contribution
sections.text: No patients or members of the public were involved in the design, conduct, analysis, interpretation, or reporting of this study. The participants were healthcare professionals.

items.title: Colours of the mind: A qualitative study exploring the relationship between neurodivergence and creativity.
items.authors: Erin B, Shaw SCK, Quadt L, Eccles JA.

sections.text: The neurodiversity movement advocates for a societal framework that recognises neurodivergence as a difference, rather than a disorder. Despite the advocacy efforts, neurodivergent people still face issues with their physical and mental health at higher rates than the general population. Some scholars argue that these disproportionate rates originate from stress resulting from discrimination and societal stigma faced by neurodivergent people. This study aims to challenge these societal views through exploring one of the reported strengths of being neurodivergent: creativity. This study aims to explore why neurodivergent populations may be creative. To research this complex relationship between being neurodivergence and creativity a qualitative study was conducted. Ten neurodivergent adults who had studied or were currently studying a creative degree were interviewed on Zoom, exploring their beliefs about this relationship. An inductive thematic analysis was then carried out. The analysis gave rise to three themes: (1) The Construct of Creativity, (2) Resilience, & (3) Empowerment. These themes provided hypotheses for understanding the connection between neurodivergence and creativity. The results provided two hypotheses. The 'innate trait hypothesis' posits that traits thought to be intrinsic to neurodivergence may be beneficial in fostering creativity. The innate traits that arose were divergent thinking, monotropism and communication differences. The 'social isolation hypothesis' posits that the discrimination that neurodivergent people face leads to profound isolation and in some cases mental health challenges. Neurodivergent people may then use creativity as a method for regulating their emotions, providing solace from distress. Moreover, the isolation they experience provides an opportunity for introspection, which fuels creativity. Our results highlight that some neurodivergent traits, when placed within a creative context, can become strengths. This highlights the possibility that the pathologisation of neurodivergent traits is not just damaging but also invalid, with the reality being much more nuanced.

items.title: Readability of online information on nature and mental health.
items.authors: Agbonlahor O, Vincent K, Wood LA, Tomlinson MM, Kerstiens S, Clarke J, McLeish AC, Walker KL, Hart JL.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Associations between exposure to nature and positive mental health outcomes have been established. Although the Internet is a popular source of accessing mental health information, little is known about the readability of such online information. Thus, the goal of this study was to assess the readability of online information regarding the association between exposure to nature and mental health.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A search of webpages was conducted using the following search terms: 'mental health and urban greening', 'stress and urban greening', 'mental health and nature', 'stress and nature', 'mental health and outdoors', and 'stress and outdoors'. Readability of the 255 webpages identified was determined by the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level measure.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: On average, webpage content was written at an 11th grade reading level (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level mean=11.95, SD=2.68), and fewer than 2% of webpages met readability guidelines (i.e. ≤6th grade reading level).

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Most online content related to nature and mental health should be written at a more appropriate level for general audiences. Web content developers should prioritize adherence to readability guidelines.

items.title: Associations of vitamin status and T-lymphocyte subsets with tic severity in children: a cross-sectional study using the Yale Global Tic Severity Scale.
items.authors: Zhu F, Gao Y, Zhang Z, Kang S, Xu W, Zhang J.

sections.text: Vitamin D insufficiency and immune dysregulation have been implicated in tic disorders; however, the relationship between vitamin status, peripheral T-lymphocyte subsets, and tic severity in children remains incompletely defined. We aimed to evaluate associations between serum vitamin indices, peripheral lymphocyte subsets, and tic severity, measured by the Yale Global Tic Severity Scale (YGTSS) global severity score, in newly diagnosed children with tic disorders. This single-center cross-sectional study included children aged <14 years with newly diagnosed, treatment-naive tic disorders who attended Zhangjiagang Hospital affiliated to Soochow University/The First People's Hospital of Zhangjiagang City between January 2022 and August 2025. The YGTSS global severity score was calculated as the sum of the total tic score and impairment score. Normality was assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test. Associations were examined using Spearman correlation with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction and adjusted linear regression with HC3 robust standard errors. Vitamin D groups were compared using the Kruskal-Wallis test followed by Dunn-Bonferroni pairwise tests. Analyses were performed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27.0 and R version 4.4.2. In total, 41 children were included (29 male and 12 female participants; mean age, 8.61 ± 2.70 years). The mean YGTSS global severity score was 30.71 ± 10.25. CD4+ T-cell absolute count showed the strongest inverse correlation with the YGTSS global severity score (Spearman ρ = -0.474, P = 0.0017; FDR-adjusted P = 0.0260). After adjustment for age, sex, and disease duration, the association remained significant using HC3 robust standard errors (B = -0.018, 95% CI -0.031 to -0.005; P = 0.0069). The overall difference among vitamin D groups was significant (Kruskal-Wallis P = 0.0073); Dunn-Bonferroni testing identified a difference only between the <20- and 20- to <30-ng/mL groups (adjusted P = 0.0077). Lower peripheral CD4+ T-cell absolute count remained associated with greater tic-related symptom burden after covariate adjustment in children with tic disorders. Vitamin D findings were exploratory, did not show a monotonic dose-response pattern, and were less robust than the CD4+ T-cell association. Larger prospective studies are needed.

items.title: Comprehensive management of chronic insomnia in Spain: a multidisciplinary modified RAND/UCLA consensus with recommendations on daridorexant.
items.authors: Álvarez-Ruiz-Larrinaga A, Armenteros L, Bellido C, Triguero LL, Martínez-Raga J, Pascual J, San L.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Chronic insomnia is a prevalent 24-hour disorder with significant daytime impact. Its management is frequently complicated by conceptual barriers, limited use of standardised diagnostic tools and prolonged benzodiazepine use, while insomnia is often overlooked or inadequately coded as an independent disorder. These challenges highlight the need for improved recognition and clearer therapeutic pathways. Dual orexin receptor antagonists (DORAs), particularly daridorexant, offer a new pharmacological option targeting wake-promoting pathways, yet practical guidance on their clinical use remains limited.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: A multidisciplinary panel of seven experts conducted a national consensus using the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method. Seventy-four statements addressing the nature, diagnosis and treatment of chronic insomnia, including the clinical use of daridorexant, were evaluated across two rating rounds and a structured discussion. Consensus was reached on 36 statements in round one; one statement was removed; and the remaining 37 achieved consensus in round two.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Experts agreed that chronic insomnia is a distinct disorder, with hyperarousal as a central mechanism, and emphasised the importance of targeting daytime functioning and preserving sleep architecture. Daridorexant was considered appropriate across heterogeneous clinical profiles, supported by evidence demonstrating improvements in nocturnal sleep, daytime functioning and sleep architecture, along with favourable tolerability and low abuse potential.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This consensus supports a pragmatic and patient-centred approach to chronic insomnia management, integrating current evidence with expert clinical experience. The recommendations may help guide decision-making in routine practice, including the use of daridorexant when pharmacological treatment is considered appropriate.
