items.title: Physical activity and body dissatisfaction among female university students: a three-wave study of psychological flexibility and resilience.
items.authors: Zhang Y, Liu Z, Hu C, Lu L.

sections.text: Body dissatisfaction (BD) is a common psychological concern among female university students. Although physical activity (PA) has been associated with more favourable body-related evaluations, the psychological factors that may account for this association remain unclear. This study examined the independent and theoretically ordered indirect associations of psychological flexibility (PF) and psychological resilience (PR) in the prospective association between PA and BD. A three-wave prospective study was conducted among 1,086 first- and second-year female university students from three universities in China. Assessments were administered at 6-month intervals over 12 months. The hypothesised statistical model included T1 PA, T2 PF, and T3 PR and BD. PF was operationalized as lower experiential avoidance, with lower experiential avoidance representing greater PF. Only-child status, BMI category, and self-rated health were included as covariates. Indirect associations were estimated using PROCESS Model 6 with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. T1 PA was positively associated with T2 PF (β = 0.419, p <.001) and T3 PR (β = 0.239, p <.001), while T2 PF was positively associated with T3 PR (β = 0.434, p <.001). T1 PA, T2 PF, and T3 PR were each negatively associated with T3 BD (β = -0.127, -0.225, and -0.355, respectively; all p <.001). The total indirect association was significant (β = -0.243, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.280, -0.206]). Significant specific indirect associations were observed through PF (β = -0.094, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.121, -0.069]), through PR (β = -0.085, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.109, -0.061]), and through the theoretically ordered PF-PR sequence (β = -0.064, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.081, -0.050]). Higher PA was prospectively associated with lower subsequent BD, with significant theoretically ordered indirect associations involving lower experiential avoidance, operationalized as greater PF, and greater PR. These findings highlight the potential relevance of adaptive psychological resources in understanding the prospective association between PA and BD among female university students.

Assessments were administered at 6-month intervals over 12 months. The hypothesised statistical model included T1 PA, T2 PF, and T3 PR and BD. PF was operationalized as lower experiential avoidance, with lower experiential avoidance representing greater PF. Only-child status, BMI category, and self-rated health were included as covariates. Indirect associations were estimated using PROCESS Model 6 with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. T1 PA was positively associated with T2 PF (β = 0.419, p <.001) and T3 PR (β = 0.239, p <.001), while T2 PF was positively associated with T3 PR (β = 0.434, p <.001). T1 PA, T2 PF, and T3 PR were each negatively associated with T3 BD (β = -0.127, -0.225, and -0.355, respectively; all p <.001). The total indirect association was significant (β = -0.243, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.280, -0.206]). Higher PA was prospectively associated with lower subsequent BD, with significant theoretically ordered indirect associations involving lower experiential avoidance, operationalized as greater PF, and greater PR. These findings highlight the potential relevance of adaptive psychological resources in understanding the prospective association between PA and BD among female university students.

items.title: Psychological resilience and burnout in nursing interns versus registered nurses: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.authors: Chen X, Zhang Y, Zhang F, Zhu X.

sections.text: Burnout is a common, serious occupational mental-health problem in nursing, and psychological resilience is a modifiable factor that may be associated with lower burnout. Whether this association holds equally across the education-to-practice transition, from interns to registered nurses, is unclear, and the most comparable prior meta-analysis excluded nursing students and the Chinese-language literature. We aimed to pool the resilience-burnout association in nurses and nursing interns. Two coprimary outcomes were prespecified: the resilience-emotional-exhaustion (EE) correlation, and a concept-matched intern-versus-registered-nurse comparison on total burnout. Secondary outcomes were depersonalization and personal accomplishment. Nine databases, five English-language and four Chinese-language, were searched from inception to 2026 with no language filter applied inside any database; eligibility was limited to reports published in English or Chinese. Eligible studies were cross-sectional and reported a correlation between a validated resilience measure and burnout in nurses or nursing interns. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and appraised quality (AHRQ 11-item). Correlations were pooled via Fisher's z under random-effects models (REML; metafor), with subgroup, sensitivity, and small-study analyses. Seventy-eight occupational-burnout studies were analyzed (29,292 participants); five academic-burnout studies were out of scope. Resilience was inversely associated with emotional exhaustion (r = - 0.36, 95% CI = - 0.42 to - 0.31; k = 49; I2 = 95%), total burnout (- 0.44), and depersonalization (- 0.30), and positively associated with personal accomplishment (+ 0.43). On the concept-matched comparison (total burnout), registered nurses showed a numerically stronger association than interns (r = - 0.46 vs. - 0.28; Q_between p = 0.025); with only five intern studies and instability in sensitivity analyses, this difference is preliminary. Estimates were stable across leave-one-out, model-choice, and PET-PEESE analyses, and no weaker in the nine studies scoring AHRQ ≥ 8 (r = - 0.43, - 0.59 to - 0.24); no funnel-plot asymmetry was detected (Egger's p = 0.49). Psychological resilience is a moderate, consistent protective correlate of nurse burnout, but a wide prediction interval reflecting high heterogeneity means its practical benefit likely varies across settings. Resilience-building should complement, not replace, organizational measures. Whether the correlate is stronger in registered nurses than in interns remains preliminary. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261427008, identifier CRD420261427008.

items.title: Exploring the association between loneliness and breastfeeding duration in Chinese primiparas.
items.authors: Zhang H, Zeng P, Chen M, Liu R, Fu M, Wei H, Chen S, Wu H.

sections.text: Reaching the recommendations for exclusive breastfeeding (EBF) during the first 6 months postpartum remains a worldwide challenge. Meanwhile, Chinese primiparas suffered from the loneliness associated with the traditional practice of zuoyuezi and the isolation during the COVID-19 pandemic. As far as we know, little is known about whether there is the association between loneliness in Chinese primiparas and breastfeeding duration. This study aimed to explore whether loneliness in Chinese primiparas was associated with reduced breastfeeding duration, and further to explore the endocrine mechanisms. The Chinese primiparas were assessed for loneliness using the Los Angeles Loneliness Scale (R-UCLA) within 7-14 days postpartum. According to the scores of R-UCLA, the subjects were divided into three groups: no loneliness group (n=162), a low loneliness group (n=65) and a high loneliness group (n=40). The Postpartum Breastfeeding Questionnaire was filled out to record breastfeeding duration. The expression levels of the serum lactation hormone(prolactin)and the stress hormone (cortisol) were measured. The time and rate of breastfeeding initiation within 3 days postpartum, as well as the frequencies of exclusive breastfeeding at 15 and 30 days postpartum, were significantly lower in Chinese primiparas with high loneliness; specifically, High loneliness was associated with lower exclusive breastfeeding rates by 25.2% (P<0.01) within 24 hours postpartum, 19.9% (P < 0.01) at 24 to 48 hours postpartum, 22.5% (P < 0.01) at 48 to 72 hours postpartum, 39.8% (P < 0.01) at 90 days postpartum, respectively. The probability of cumulative 90- and 180-day exclusive breastfeeding was the lowest in Chinese primiparas with high loneliness. The probability of cumulative 90- and 180-day exclusive breastfeeding rates decreased as the scores on the Loneliness Scale increased. Compared with primiparas in the no-loneliness and low-loneliness groups, those in the high-loneliness group exhibited the highest expression levels of the stress hormone (serum cortisol) and the lowest expression levels of the lactation hormone (serum prolactin) at 3, 15, and 45 days postpartum, respectively. Loneliness in Chinese primiparas during lactation was associated with lower exclusive breastfeeding rates and duration.

items.title: Financially focused self-concept and problem lottery gambling: the chain mediating role of gambling-related luck beliefs and lottery gambling passion.
items.authors: Hu Y, Liu L, Bai C, Gan Z, Liu X.

sections.text: China operates the world's largest lottery market, yet the psychological mechanisms linking individual dispositions to problem lottery gambling remain insufficiently understood, particularly among mainland Chinese samples. Financially focused self-concept-the tendency to base self-worth on financial success-has been linked to gambling problems. However, the pathways linking it to problem lottery gambling have received little empirical attention. This study aimed to investigate the association between financially focused self-concept and problem lottery gambling among Chinese lottery gamblers, and the mediating roles of gambling-related luck beliefs and lottery gambling passion within this association. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among Chinese lottery gamblers recruited from land-based retail outlets. A total of 879 participants completed measures of financially focused self-concept, gambling-related luck beliefs, lottery gambling passion, and problem lottery gambling. Structural equation modelling and bias-corrected bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples were used to test the proposed mediation model. Correlation analyses showed that financially focused self-concept was positively correlated with gambling-related luck beliefs, obsessive passion, harmonious passion, and problem lottery gambling (p < 0.001). Financially focused self-concept showed a nonsignificant positive association with problem lottery gambling after accounting for the mediating variables (β = 0.03, p = 0.40). The specific indirect associations through gambling-related luck beliefs (β = 0.034, 95% CI [0.009, 0.061]), obsessive passion (β = 0.065, 95% CI [0.036, 0.097]), and harmonious passion (β = -0.010, 95% CI [-0.021, -0.001]) were all significant. The serial indirect associations via gambling-related luck beliefs and obsessive passion (β = 0.034, 95% CI [0.018, 0.054]) and via gambling-related luck beliefs and harmonious passion (β = -0.010, 95% CI [-0.019, -0.004]) were also significant. Financially focused self-concept is associated with problem lottery gambling through gambling-related luck beliefs, obsessive passion, and harmonious passion. The findings are consistent with the Pathways Model and its recent extension. They also highlight the importance of addressing luck beliefs and internalisation processes in prevention efforts targeting financially focused lottery consumers.

items.title: Peripheral serum copper metabolite levels measured by ultrafiltration aid in the clinical screening of Alzheimer's disease.
items.authors: Zhang Y, Li L, Ouyang H, Zhao Z, Mei X, Qiu C.

sections.text: The number of patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD) is increasing, yet misdiagnosis remains common and early accurate diagnosis is lacking. Previous studies have suggested abnormalities in peripheral serum copper levels in AD patients. This study sought to explore the diagnostic value of peripheral serum copper-related biomarkers for clinically diagnosed AD. Peripheral serum samples were collected from 115 clinically diagnosed AD patients and 96 healthy controls (HC). A preliminary experiment on five samples determined the use of a 10 kDa ultrafiltration membrane. Four serum copper parameters-serum total copper (tot-Cu), free copper (free-Cu), serum immunological ceruloplasmin concentration (iCp), and ceruloplasmin enzymatic activity (eCp)-were quantitatively measured in all samples using ultrafiltration, atomic absorption spectrometry, and ELISA. Peripheral tot-Cu and free-Cu levels in clinically diagnosed AD patients were significantly elevated in the early stage of the disease, while iCp, eCp, and the iCp/eCp ratio were significantly decreased. The diagnostic efficacy of tot-Cu and free-Cu for these Alzheimer's disease patients was significantly higher than that of the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score. Nevertheless, these indicators could not distinguish different severity stages of clinically phenotyped AD. Our results indicate that tot-Cu or free-Cu holds promise as biomarkers for the clinical screening of AD; peripheral copper metabolic dysregulation may be involved in the pathogenesis of clinically phenotyped AD.

items.title: Reduced causal connectivity in multiple resting-state networks in autism spectrum disorder detected by convergent cross mapping.
items.authors: Zhang H, He L, Wang D, Yan Y, He Y, Zhang Y, Shi Y, Chen Y.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: This study investigates alterations in causal connectivity within resting-state brain functional networks in patients with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) using the Convergent Cross Mapping (CCM) method.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Data were obtained from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange I (ABIDE I) public database. To minimize variability, resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) data were restricted to the NYU site, comprising 52 ASD patients and 52 matched typically developing controls. Based on the AAL template, time series were extracted from five resting-state networks: attention network, default mode network, sensorimotor network, visual network, and subcortical network. The CCM method was employed to analyze causal connectivity among these brain regions. Additionally, a support vector machine (SVM) classifier was utilized to assess the discriminative potential of the identified causal connectivity patterns.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Significant differences in causal connections were observed, particularly in the default mode network, which exhibited the most pronounced alterations. Overall, ASD patients showed a general decrease in causal connectivity across networks, accompanied by some localized increases. The SVM classifier accurately differentiated individuals with ASD from controls based on the causal connectivity patterns derived from resting-state brain networks.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: These findings elucidate dynamical network mechanisms underlying ASD pathophysiology and highlight candidate neurobiological markers with potential translational relevance.

Data were obtained from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange I (ABIDE I) public database. To minimize variability, resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) data were restricted to the NYU site, comprising 52 ASD patients and 52 matched typically developing controls. Based on the AAL template, time series were extracted from five resting-state networks: attention network, default mode network, sensorimotor network, visual network, and subcortical network. The CCM method was employed to analyze causal connectivity among these brain regions. Additionally, a support vector machine (SVM) classifier was utilized to assess the discriminative potential of the identified causal connectivity patterns.

Significant differences in causal connections were observed, particularly in the default mode network, which exhibited the most pronounced alterations. Overall, ASD patients showed a general decrease in causal connectivity across networks, accompanied by some localized increases. The SVM classifier accurately differentiated individuals with ASD from controls based on the causal connectivity patterns derived from resting-state brain networks.

These findings elucidate dynamical network mechanisms underlying ASD pathophysiology and highlight candidate neurobiological markers with potential translational relevance.

items.title: The moderating effect of cognitive re-evaluation on the relationship between superficial performance and job burnout in psychiatric nurses.
items.authors: Hong S, Huang S, Zhu M, Jin A, Zhang Q, Huang A, Wang L.

sections.text: Demand for emotional labor is increasing among psychiatric nurses who are now more at risk for job burnout, and emotional labor strategies or emotion regulation styles may be important mechanisms in this process. The purpose of this study was to investigate the relationships among emotional labor, emotion regulation, and job burnout in psychiatric nurses, and to examine cognitive reappraisal as a potential moderator of the relationship between surface acting and burnout. During January-February 2025, a cross-sectional survey was performed among on-duty nurses in a tertiary psychiatric hospital located in Zhejiang Province, China. Emotional labor, emotion regulation, job burnout, nursing professional values, perceived decent work and innovative capacity were assessed using validated Chinese scales. Descriptive statistics, correlation analyses, multiple linear regression, hierarchical moderation analysis, and simple slope analysis were performed. Regression assumptions, multicollinearity, and common method bias were additionally assessed. Of 245 returned questionnaires, 241 were included in the final analysis. After adjustment for demographic and work-related factors, surface acting was positively associated with job burnout (β = 0.416, 95% CI: 0.249-0.582, p < 0.001), whereas cognitive reappraisal was inversely associated with burnout (β = -0.419, 95% CI: -0.560 to -0.278, p < 0.001). The surface acting × cognitive reappraisal interaction was statistically significant but small (β = -0.137, 95% CI: -0.238 to -0.036, ΔR² = 0.019, f² = 0.032, p = 0.008). Higher surface acting was associated with higher job burnout, whereas higher cognitive reappraisal was associated with lower burnout. Cognitive reappraisal also showed a small moderating association, with the positive association between surface acting and burnout becoming weaker at higher levels of reappraisal. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal direction and practical relevance of these associations.

items.title: The influence of indigenous documentary narratives on cultural resilience and mental health awareness.
items.authors: Li P, Jia C, Chen Y.

sections.text: Indigenous documentary narratives may provide culturally grounded contexts for understanding identity, resilience and mental health, yet empirical evidence linking narrative engagement with these interconnected outcomes remains limited, particularly within Indigenous communities in China. This cross-sectional mixed-methods observational study examined associations among narrative engagement, perceived cultural authenticity, cultural identification, cultural resilience, mental health awareness, stigma and help-seeking attitudes among 480 adults from ethnic minority communities in Yunnan and Hunan Provinces, China, with 36 participants contributing qualitative data. After a standardized viewing session involving four documentaries representing Yi, Miao, Bai and Tujia/Miao narratives, participants completed culturally adapted measures of narrative engagement and cultural and mental-health constructs. Confirmatory factor analysis supported the final 60-item, six-factor measurement model (χ2(1,695) = 3,284.15, χ2/df = 1.937, CFI = 0.941, TLI = 0.938, RMSEA = 0.044, 95% CI [0.042, 0.046], SRMR = 0.048), with satisfactory reliability and convergent validity. Narrative engagement was positively associated with cultural resilience (r = 0.51), mental health awareness (r = 0.44), and help-seeking attitudes, while showing an inverse association with mental health stigma (r = -0.35; all p < 0.001). Multivariable models explained 53.4% of the variance in cultural resilience and 34.8% of the variance in mental health awareness. Covariate-adjusted statistical indirect associations were observed through cultural identification (β = 0.225, 95% BCa CI [0.168, 0.291]) and perceived cultural authenticity (β = 0.114, 95% CI [0.058, 0.144]). Qualitative analysis identified cultural mirroring, normalization of distress through cultural metaphors, and intergenerational dialogue as central themes. Overall, the findings identify interconnected statistical associations among narrative, cultural and mental-health variables, but do not establish temporal or causal pathways. Longitudinal and comparative studies are needed to examine the temporal stability and potential mechanisms underlying these associations.

items.title: Enhancing integration for greater sustainability of HIV, TB and malaria responses: insights and lessons from African community-led monitoring programs.
items.authors: Oberth G, Bozinovski J, Perez S.

sections.text: Global HIV, TB and malaria responses have achieved substantial gains, largely through vertical programs and parallel systems. With shrinking external funding, integration is a strategic process that supports sustainability by replacing fragmented approaches with unified models, embedded in public health systems. Community-led monitoring (CLM) provides community-generated evidence that can inform efforts to advance the integration agenda. This community case study synthesizes evidence and lessons from secondary CLM reports covering more than 4,000 health facilities in 16 African countries, according to integration focus areas for the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria. At the service level, CLM identifies persistent fragmentation, including gaps in TB/HIV co-infection services, weak coordination between programs, and patient pathways requiring multiple visits. CLM data have been used to advocate for integrated solutions, including same-day service delivery and stronger linkages between HIV, sexual and reproductive health, gender-based violence, and mental health services. CLM also provides insights into the integration of vertical programs into primary health care, particularly during donor transitions. At the systems level, CLM is being used within efforts to strengthen integration, including through unified monitoring frameworks, incorporation of community data into national systems, and improvements in supply chains, laboratories and workforce capacity. CLM data have been used to inform advocacy and decision-making related to integrated sample transportations systems, and expansion of social health insurance coverage. Key lessons highlight the importance of integrated monitoring tools, the role of community actors in facilitating integration, and the potential for CLM to contribute to broader health system reform processes.

With shrinking external funding, integration is a strategic process that supports sustainability by replacing fragmented approaches with unified models, embedded in public health systems. Community-led monitoring (CLM) provides community-generated evidence that can inform efforts to advance the integration agenda. This community case study synthesizes evidence and lessons from secondary CLM reports covering more than 4,000 health facilities in 16 African countries, according to integration focus areas for the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria. At the service level, CLM identifies persistent fragmentation, including gaps in TB/HIV co-infection services, weak coordination between programs, and patient pathways requiring multiple visits. CLM data have been used to advocate for integrated solutions, including same-day service delivery and stronger linkages between HIV, sexual and reproductive health, gender-based violence, and mental health services. CLM also provides insights into the integration of vertical programs into primary health care, particularly during donor transitions. At the systems level, CLM is being used within efforts to strengthen integration, including through unified monitoring frameworks, incorporation of community data into national systems, and improvements in supply chains, laboratories and workforce capacity. CLM data have been used to inform advocacy and decision-making related to integrated sample transportations systems, and expansion of social health insurance coverage. Key lessons highlight the importance of integrated monitoring tools, the role of community actors in facilitating integration, and the potential for CLM to contribute to broader health system reform processes.

items.title: Quality, reliability, and stigmatizing content of sexual and gender minority health videos on Chinese short-form video platforms.
items.authors: Hu H, Yu Z, Yang F.

sections.text: Sexual and gender minority (SGM) populations increasingly rely on digital platforms for health information, yet the quality, reliability, and stigmatizing content of SGM health videos remain unclear. This study evaluated SGM health-related short-form videos on the Chinese platforms Douyin and Bilibili. We conducted a cross-sectional content analysis of prominently ranked videos retrieved using 15 research-team-developed search terms during the prespecified data-collection period (January 1-May 1, 2026). For each search term, the first 10 results returned under each platform's default ranking were recorded, yielding 150 candidate records per platform before deduplication. Eligible videos were assessed for uploader type, content theme, engagement metrics, Global Quality Score (GQS), modified DISCERN reliability, medical accuracy, misinformation, and an exploratory stigma-to-affirmation communication score. Non-parametric tests, Cramér's V with 95% confidence intervals, and unadjusted Spearman correlations were used. Of 300 candidate records, 194 videos were included (118 Douyin, 76 Bilibili). Individual users and healthcare professionals were the most common uploaders. HIV/STI prevention and mental health were the leading themes, whereas healthcare access, privacy protection, HPV vaccination, and cancer screening were underrepresented. Overall quality was moderate [median GQS = 3.0; interquartile range (IQR), 2.0-4.0], but reliability was limited (median modified DISCERN = 2.0; IQR, 1.0-3.0). High-quality and highly reliable videos accounted for 38.1% and 19.1%, respectively. Misinformation appeared in 27.8% of videos, and 17.0% contained stigmatizing, pathologizing, fear-based, or discriminatory elements. Raw cumulative engagement metrics were strongly intercorrelated but showed weak unadjusted associations with quality, reliability, accuracy, or the exploratory communication score. Among prominently ranked SGM health videos identified using the predefined search strategy, overall quality was moderate, reliability was limited, thematic coverage was uneven, and misinformation and stigmatizing communication remained present. Raw engagement metrics showed weak associations with quality-related scores. These findings describe a time-bounded algorithmic snapshot and should not be generalized to all content on either platform.
